title: 골프웨어, ‘브랜드 양극화’ 더 짙어졌다…지포어 9개점 1위
title_ko: 골프웨어, ‘브랜드 양극화’ 더 짙어졌다…지포어 9개점 1위
summary: 골프웨어 시장이 장기화된 소비 둔화 속에서도 브랜드별·점포별 성과가 극명하게 갈리는 양상을 보이고 있다. 주요 백화점 12개 점포의 최근 매출 실적을 살펴보면 ‘지포어’가 9개 점포에서 1위를 차지하며 독주 체제를 이어간 가운데 말본골프와 타이틀리스트가 뒤를 받쳤다. 반면 같은 브랜드라도 점포에 따라 두 자릿수 성장과 역신장이 엇갈리면서 골프웨어 시장의 경쟁축이 단순한 브랜드 인지도에서 상권별 고객 적중도와 상품 경쟁력으로 이동하고 있다.특히 눈에 띄는 것은 상위 브랜드 쏠림과 신흥 브랜드의 약진이 동시에 나타나고 있다는 점이다.

title: 최병오 회장 연임 출마 여부 ‘분수령’
summary: 섬유산업연합회 반세기 역사상 경천동지할 흑역사로 기록될 8·7 섬산련 회장 선출 파동이 일시 수면 아래의 잠복기를 끝내고 “타협이냐” “대립이냐”의 선택지를 놓고 치열한 수 싸움을 예고하고 있다.8·7 섬산련 총회에서 최병오 회장 연임 안건이 표류해 차기 이사회에 5인 추대위 선정을 미루고 찬·반 양 진영 간 일단 휴전에 들어가 숙려기간이 진행되고 있다.최 회장의 임기가 다시 6개월 자동 연장돼 내년 2월17일로 미뤄지자 최회장 지지와 반대 진영 모두 차기 이사회 일정이 잡혀질때까지 “아무일 없었다”는 식으로 평온을 유지하고 있다.

content: NEW YORK, NY — August 5, 2026 — Carnegie, a supplier of sustainable textiles and acoustical management solutions for the commercial industry, introduces Aperture Embroider, a new textile design as part of the new Crush Collection. As Carnegie’s latest addition to its Biobased Xorel product line, Aperture Embroider is made with rapidly renewable materials and 91% plant-based content, delivering durability, cleanability, and finish-free construction that Biobased Xorel is known for. Aperture Embroider, new design part of the Crush Collection | Courtesy of Carnegie Aperture Embroider brings a sense of movement and light to Biobased Xorel through finely stitched, radial bursts that feel almost like sparks across the surface. The embroidered detail adds a layer of dimension and tactility, while the open ground keeps it airy and versatile. As part of the Crush collection, Aperture Embroider is part of a lineup of fabrics created for designers who lead with color. From bold graphics and plush velvets to expressive florals, Crush was designed to mix, layer, and play, signaling Carnegie’s shift toward a brighter, bolder aesthetic while maintaining its commitment to responsible materials. Free of added finishes and harmful chemicals, Aperture Embroider is available in four colorways suited for wallcovering, upholstered walls/panels, and upholstery, pairing expressive design with the performance and sustainability standards Carnegie is known for. Rated for 200,000 double rubs and cleanable with water-, solvent-, and bleach-based solutions, the fabric exceeds Type II criteria for wallcovering performance. title: Lectra Strengthens Its Partnership With Caron Technology
summary: PARIS — September 3, 2026 — Lectra announces the strengthening of its industrial alliance with Caron Technology, an Italian company founded in 1993 and specializing in preparation systems operating before the cutting process. This new milestone reflects the strength of a trusted relationship that has grown between the two companies over nearly two decades. Lectra, […]
content: PARIS — September 3, 2026 — Lectra announces the strengthening of its industrial alliance with Caron Technology, an Italian company founded in 1993 and specializing in preparation systems operating before the cutting process. This new milestone reflects the strength of a trusted relationship that has grown between the two companies over nearly two decades. Lectra, a catalyst for transformation in the fashion, furniture, and automotive industries, unites human expertise with cutting-edge industrial intelligence to offer technological solutions combining software in SaaS mode, cutting equipment, data, and associated services. As long-standing partners, Lectra and Caron Technology collaborate to accompany manufacturers in the fashion, automotive, and furniture industries to optimize the preparation of their cutting operations. Caron Technology designs and assembles preparation systems operating before the cutting process for flexible materials: fabric spreaders, feeders, roll loaders, spreading tables, and associated software. Upstream of the cutting process, fabric spreading and feeding are a strategic step in the production process, as the quality and consistency of these operations have a direct impact on cutting room productivity. An industrial alliance underpinned by a long-term commitment To support this new phase of development, Lectra acquired 70% of Caron Technology’s equity in August 2026 for 1.9 million euros, with an option to increase its stake to 100% by 2029. This reflects the two companies’ shared commitment to build on their cooperation over the long-term and to jointly support their future growth. content: MUSCATINE, IA. — August 23, 2026 — Allsteel is moving materiality from aesthetics to engineering with Levra , its newest task chair designed for the way people work today. Developed in collaboration with ITO Design, Levra’s ergonomic engineering is cloaked in human-centric materials and anchored by a first-of-its-kind, patent-pending frameless back architecture featuring structural knit material. Through this blend of textile innovation and ergonomic features, Levra presents a vision for the future of task seating—one where high performance and refined aesthetics merge to match the uncompromising demands of the modern workplace. What Makes Levra’s Back Special? During its development, the knit material of Levra’s back was treated as a design tool to help deliver structural integrity, adaptive flexibility, and a lighter visual expression: A suspended back softens the hard visual and physical edges of a traditional frame, while integrated lumbar support provides tactile feedback and comfort without restricting motion. The back is constructed through a precision-knit zero-waste manufacturing process. It is “fit-to-knit” directly to the chair’s specifications, entirely eliminating knit fabric cutting scrap. The knit material used in Levra’s back is made from 100% recycled materials, including up to 96% post-consumer polyester and up to 4% SEAQUAL® yarn made from upcycled marine litter. Its curated, monochromatic color palette and refined silhouette integrate seamlessly into design-forward interiors, offering a high-performance seating option that complements the visual language of modern office spaces. title: Bangladesh needs energy resilience strategy to safeguard RMG
summary: Key insights A 450 mmcfd gas shock cut 17% of Bangladesh’s gas supply. LNG spot prices have more than doubled to $24–$25/MMBtu. Domestic gas decline, limited offshore progress, and slow CBM commercia...
content: Key insights A 450 mmcfd gas shock cut 17% of Bangladesh’s gas supply. LNG spot prices have more than doubled to $24–$25/MMBtu. Domestic gas decline, limited offshore progress, and slow CBM commercialization make supply diversification essential but largely medium- to long-term. Bangladesh’s 7.63 TCF gas reserves provide only about 12 years of supply. RMG exports fell 1.64% to $38.7 billion in FY2025–26. Factory-level energy efficiency and fiscal policy reform are immediate bridges to protect export margins. Figure: The government has launched an Offshore Bidding Round for 24 offshore blocks, including 9 shallow-sea and 15 deep-sea blocks. Bangladesh’s ready-made garment (RMG) sector is facing an acute operational crisis. Severe energy shortages have disrupted spinning, knitting, dyeing, and captive-power operations across major manufacturing hubs. The immediate challenge is to build an industry that is more productive, energy-resilient, and capable of producing higher-value products. The supply chain disruptions of July and August 2026 have exposed a structural weakness. Low-cost volume manufacturing cannot remain competitive without reliable energy to run boilers, process textiles, and meet delivery schedules. Gas crisis becomes an industrial crisis The crisis began on July 21 when a fire and control system fault disabled Excelerate Energy’s floating LNG terminal off Moheshkhali. The outage removed 450 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd) from the national grid, eliminating 17% of total gas supply. Bangladesh was already operating below its daily demand of 3,800 to 4,000 mmcfd, while domestic fields produced only 2,366 mmcfd. title: ALLIED Feather + Down Finds 85% Lower Carbon Emissions Than Estimated Down Industry Average
summary: MONTEBELLO, CA — September 3, 2026 — ALLIED Feather + Down, a global supplier of responsibly sourced and sustainably processed down, today announced the results of a recent carbon footprint audit conducted at their facility in Hangzhou, China. Results reported by Green Threads DPP show that ALLIED’s cradle-to-gate down processing generates 85% less carbon emissions […]
content: MONTEBELLO, CA — September 3, 2026 — ALLIED Feather + Down, a global supplier of responsibly sourced and sustainably processed down, today announced the results of a recent carbon footprint audit conducted at their facility in Hangzhou, China. Results reported by Green Threads DPP show that ALLIED’s cradle-to-gate down processing generates 85% less carbon emissions than the estimated industry average. This audit focuses specifically on down processing, using actual facility and supply chain data to quantify its carbon footprint. The result gives brands a more specific benchmark for evaluating the carbon impact of the down they source and the processes used to prepare it for finished products. “We’ve known for years that down plays an important role in building a more circular and lower-impact apparel value chain,” said Daniel Uretsky, President of ALLIED Feather + Down. “These audited results allow us to put real numbers behind that belief. The data shows that our processing methods deliver a dramatically lower carbon footprint than other down providers, giving brands objective information they can use when making material decisions.” The audit found that ALLIED’s processing methods generated 0.48 Kg CO₂e per KG of down*, about 85% lower than estimated industry averages (3.2 Kg CO2e per Kg) for conventional down and 57.9% lower than published figures (1.14 Kg CO2e per Kg) for recycled down.** The audit also found that the carbon footprint of ALLIED’s down is 95% lower than the estimated carbon footprint of polyester fibers used in alternative insulations.*** Conducted by supply chain carbon audit experts Green Threads DPP, the audit evaluated greenhouse gas emissions associated with ALLIED’s down processing operation including the slaughterhouse impact, transportation a

Mr. Nilesh Ved, Chairman of APPCORP Holding, Owner of Apparel Group and Founder of KORA Properties and Patrick Lasfargues, ED Carrefour The opening marks a defining milestone in Apparel Group’s India growth journey and its expansion into food and hypermarket retail. Bringing together Carrefour’s international retail expertise and Apparel Group’s deep understanding of the Indian market, the partnership sets the foundation for a new generation of modern retail in India, built around quality, value, convenience and the evolving aspirations of Indian consumers. Spanning more than 50,000+ sq. ft., the Greater Noida flagship introduces Carrefour’s established retail experience to India through a proposition thoughtfully adapted for the local market. The store features more than 15,000+ SKUs, including exclusive international products, alongside an extensive selection of locally sourced products across fresh produce, grocery, bakery, household essentials and personal care. More than a first store, the flagship signals the scale of the ambition ahead. Apparel Group plans to expand Carrefour’s presence across North India over the coming years, building a nationwide retail platform supported by strong local partnerships, modern supply chain capabilities and an integrated omnichannel ecosystem. title: Nearly 150 Years In The Making: Environmental Textile Products (ETP) Launches New Brand Identity
title_ko: 약 150년의 제작 과정: 환경 섬유 제품(ETP), 새로운 브랜드 아이덴티티 출시
summary: MOBILE, AL — September 2, 2026 — What began as Brown & Brown, a fabric and textile business founded on the Gulf Coast in 1877 and developed into Engineered Textile Fabrics in 1980, has spent nearly 150 years growing, adapting, and expanding into markets its founders could not have imagined. content: MOBILE, AL — September 2, 2026 — What began as Brown & Brown, a fabric and textile business founded on the Gulf Coast in 1877 and developed into Engineered Textile Fabrics in 1980, has spent nearly 150 years growing, adapting, and expanding into markets its founders could not have imagined. Today, that company — now known as Environmental Textile Products (ETP) — is marking its next chapter with a new name, a unified brand identity, and a new website at EnvironmentalTextileProducts.com. The ETP family of brands — Environmental Textile Products, ETP Environmental, ETP ArtCraft Awnings, ETP Sports, ETP Racemarks, and ETP Industrial — united under one identity for the first time. The formal adoption of the Environmental Textile Products name reflects the full scope of the company’s evolution over the past several decades. From its roots in cut-and-sew manufacturing, ETP has expanded to serve customers across five distinct markets: environmental and containment systems, industrial fabric solutions, ArtCraft Awnings, Racemarks, and competitive track and field through ETP Sports, a specialized brand serving the high school, collegiate, and elite racing community. The new brand unites all five divisions under one identity for the first time, giving customers and partners a clearer picture of the company’s reach and capabilities. “This company has been in our family for five generations, and in that time, we’ve expanded into markets and capabilities that go well beyond where we started,” said Ken Robinson, owner of Environmental Textile Products. “The new name and brand reflect everything we do and everything we’ve built. title: PerkinElmer Completes Acquisition Of SimoTech
summary: SHELTON, CT — September 3, 2026 — PerkinElmer, a global supplier of analytical solutions and specialized services for the life sciences, applied, and food markets, today announced the completion of its acquisition of SimoTech, a trusted provider of manufacturing automation and GMP IT solutions to the life sciences industry, following the company’s announcement of the […]
content: SHELTON, CT — September 3, 2026 — PerkinElmer, a global supplier of analytical solutions and specialized services for the life sciences, applied, and food markets, today announced the completion of its acquisition of SimoTech, a trusted provider of manufacturing automation and GMP IT solutions to the life sciences industry, following the company’s announcement of the signed transaction on August 11, 2026. Founded in 2011 and headquartered in Cork, Ireland, SimoTech has evolved into one of the leading automation and manufacturing technology services providers in the biopharmaceutical market, supporting half of the world’s top 20 pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies. SimoTech collaborates with life sciences organizations to develop, implement, and manage automation and digital manufacturing solutions that accelerate project execution, enhance operational performance, and increase manufacturing flexibility, while ensuring regulatory compliance. This acquisition marks an expansion of PerkinElmer’s solutions for the life sciences industry, which include OneSource integrated laboratory and digital solutions as well as Project Farma’s manufacturing and engineering solutions platform. It further reinforces PerkinElmer’s standing as a premier provider of life sciences services that help accelerate research, development and the manufacturing of life-saving treatments. “By combining SimoTech’s expertise in manufacturing automation and digital systems with the capabilities of OneSource and Project Farma, this acquisition creates a significant opportunity to build a differentiated, scaled platform for pharmaceutical services,” said Michael Stubblefield, Chief Executive Officer, PerkinElmer. “We are excited to welcome SimoTech’s exceptional team to the PerkinElmer family.” “The

content: With UMT, Freudenberg Performance Materials becomes a full-service provider of advanced wound care. Source: ©Freudenberg Performance Materials Weinheim, Germany-based Freudenberg Performance Materials has acquired Foshan United Medical Ltd., a China-based supplier of advanced wound-care products. Foshan United Medical, headquartered in Foshan, China, employs about 200 people. The purchase price was not disclosed. The sellers were UMT founder and CEO Dr. Xiaodong Wang and a private Chinese founding partner. “Freudenberg Performance Materials and Foshan United Medical are a perfect strategic match,” said Dr. Andreas Raps, CEO of Freudenberg Performance Materials. “Going forward, the merger will enable us to offer a unique portfolio of technologies and products as an innovative full-service supplier in the market for advanced wound care.” UMT’s capabilities span fiber manufacturing and functionalization, nonwoven production, final packaging, sterilization and marketing authorization. Its portfolio includes polyurethane foam dressings, silicone-coated dressings, antimicrobial dressings containing silver, alginate-based absorbent fibers, and chitosan- and CMC-based wound dressings. “The innovative strength and high level of customer-orientation characteristics in both our companies make for an ideal fit,” Wang said. 2026 Quarterly Issue III

title: How Soon Could The Verticalisation Of AI Come For Fashion?
summary: AI labs continue to push the frontier of general purpose “computer use”, but verticalisation of processes remains the key to deeper domain adoption. And a new hardware interface standard could represent a different way in. The post How Soon Could The Verticalisation Of AI Come For Fashion? appeared first on The Interline .
content: Key Takeaways: Industry-agnostic, agentic “computer use” has become one of the most visible frontiers for AI development and deployment in the enterprise, but knowledge work in fashion represents a very broad spectrum of sector-specific processes, making it a hard target for automation. In easier, consumer-facing scenarios, new “blueprints” from model makers are being aimed at shrinking the gap between what language models are broadly capable of, and what they can specifically do for retail. In more complex situations, where software and hardware intersect, a new standard from Anthropic (MHS) aims to do for machinery what the Model Context Protocol (MCP) has accomplished for software, and give AI models the tools to take actions far beyond their direct purview. title: New pay scale, new wage pressure on Bangladesh’s RMG industry
summary: Inflation in Bangladesh has been eroding people's real incomes for a long time. In this reality, the new pay scale of government officials and employees is undoubtedly a necessary step. But with this,...
content: Inflation in Bangladesh has been eroding people's real incomes for a long time. In this reality, the new pay scale of government officials and employees is undoubtedly a necessary step. But with this, a big question has also come to the fore: what will happen to private-sector employees, especially RMG workers, if government employees' incomes increase? Courtesy: Collected In the recently approved new national pay scale, the minimum basic salary has been increased from 8,250 taka to 20,000 taka and the maximum basic salary from 78,000 taka to 1,56,000 taka. That is, the level of increase in the lower grades is very significant. This decision is logical considering the real income loss of government employees due to inflation for many years. But the problem is that a large part of the economy is outside this salary structure. New wage pressure may arise Currently, inflation is around 9 percent. As a result, after the increase in government salaries, it is natural for the demand for salary adjustment to increase in the private sector as well. When a private sector worker with the same qualifications and experience sees a significant increase in salary in government jobs, his or her own salary expectations will also increase. Organizations may have to increase salaries to retain skilled workers. Those who cannot will risk losing employees. The problem is that the government's salary increase comes from the budget, but private sector organizations have to pay for additional salaries from business income. They then have three main options: increase product prices, reduce profits, or increase productivity. title: Why every profitable factory still needs a lean expert
summary: Profitability is not proof of operational excellenceMany organizations assume that if the business is making money, their processes must be working well. While profitability is certainly a positive si...
content: Profitability is not proof of operational excellence Many organizations assume that if the business is making money, their processes must be working well. While profitability is certainly a positive sign, it often masks hidden inefficiencies that silently erode margins, reduce competitiveness, and limit future growth. The most successful companies don't wait for problems to appear. They improve while they are winning. The hidden cost of success A profitable factory can still be losing a significant amount of money every single day through waste that goes unnoticed. These losses rarely appear as a single large expense. Instead, they accumulate in small, everyday activities: Excess inventory occupying valuable space and cash Long machine changeover times reducing available production hours Frequent equipment breakdowns disrupting schedules Unnecessary movement by operators Waiting between processes Rework, defects, and quality failures Poor information flow causing delays and confusion These issues gradually increase operational costs while reducing customer satisfaction and overall competitiveness. The danger is that organizations become comfortable because the financial results still look healthy. The dangerous assumption One of the most common beliefs in manufacturing is: "We're making money, so our processes must be good." Unfortunately, this assumption prevents organizations from seeing improvement opportunities. Many factories only begin their Lean journey after profits decline, customer complaints increase, or competition becomes stronger. By then, valuable time and money have already been lost. summary: South Korean materials manufacturer Unichem is acquiring US flexible electronics specialist Loomia Technologies as it looks to move into tactile sensing systems for humanoid robots and smart automotive interiors. The deal follows Loomia’s collaboration with Chinese automotive technology and manufacturing group R&Y on a new flexible tactile sensor designed to detect both vertical pressure and […] The post Unichem acquires Loomia appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: South Korean materials manufacturer Unichem is acquiring US flexible electronics specialist Loomia Technologies as it looks to move into tactile sensing systems for humanoid robots and smart automotive interiors. The deal follows Loomia’s collaboration with Chinese automotive technology and manufacturing group R&Y on a new flexible tactile sensor designed to detect both vertical pressure and shear forces – the lateral forces generated when an object moves across a surface. Such multi-directional sensing is considered important for humanoid robotic hands and grippers, where detecting pressure alone provides only limited information about how securely an object is being held. Loomia and R&Y are targeting the delivery of a first engineering sample of the new sensor in January 2027, with Tesla Optimus, OpenAI, Boston Dynamics, 1X and Meta among the global robotics and AI companies identified as potential customers for the technology. Based in Ansan, Gyeonggi Province, South Korea, Unichem has around 50 years of experience in natural leather and other materials and is an established supplier of automotive interior materials. It has agreed to acquire 100% of Brooklyn, New York-based Loomia in a transaction valued at up to $6.3 million. The acquisition is expected to combine Unichem’s materials processing expertise with Loomia’s flexible electronics technology and R&Y’s automotive-scale engineering and manufacturing capabilities. summary: Industry leaders, academics, and representatives from the apparel buying community gathered yesterday (September 2) at the Bangladesh-China Friendship Exhibition Center, Purbachal, Dhaka, for a time...
content: Industry leaders, academics, and representatives from the apparel buying community gathered yesterday (September 2) at the Bangladesh-China Friendship Exhibition Center, Purbachal, Dhaka, for a timely discussion on building a stronger innovation ecosystem for Bangladesh’s textile and apparel industry. The session, titled “Building Innovation Ecosystem for a Sustainable Textile & Apparel Industry,” was held as part of TexTIMe – Textile Today’s Episode 29 and the 7th episode of the Series of Exhibitions 2026, concurrently with the 25th Textech Bangladesh 2026 International Expo and the 53rd Dye+Chem Bangladesh International Expo 2026. Figure 1: Panelists of TexTIME Episode 29. The session brought together key stakeholders from industry, academia, technology and buying houses to discuss the evolving needs of Bangladesh’s textile and apparel sector and the importance of innovation in securing its future competitiveness. The panel featured Dr. Md. Hasib Uddin, Director, BGMEA and Managing Director, APS Knit Composite Ltd.; Mohammad Rashed, Vice Chairman, BKMEA and Managing Director of Pacific Sweater Ltd.; Prof. Dr. Engr. Ayub Nabi Khan, Vice Chancellor, BGMEA University of Fashion & Technology (BUFT); and Mohammed Zakir Hossain, Senior Vice President, Bangladesh Garment Buying House Association (BGBA) and Chairman, TexSolution Consulting Bangladesh Ltd. The discussion was moderated by Dr. Mohammad Hasan, Managing Director, Cotton Group and Executive Editor, Textile Today, who also delivered the keynote address. The event highlighted the growing importance of creating stronger connections among industry, academia, technology providers and other stakeholders to drive innovation across the textile and apparel value chain. title: Textile waste recycling machine market to reach $7.1 billion by 2034
summary: The global textile waste recycling machine market was about $4.6 billion in 2023. It is projected to reach $7.1 billion by 2034. Manufacturers and recyclers are investing more in circular production....
content: The global textile waste recycling machine market was about $4.6 billion in 2023. It is projected to reach $7.1 billion by 2034. Manufacturers and recyclers are investing more in circular production. According to Transparency Market Research, the market is expected to grow at a 4.0% compound annual growth rate (CAGR) from 2024 to 2034. Figure: Investment is expected to focus on automated sorting, high-capacity recycling systems, and fiber-recovery technologies.Courtesy: Collected Textile recycling machines process yarn waste, fabric waste, carpets, and other textile materials into reusable fibers. These recovered fibers can be used in rotor spinning and nonwoven production, helping reduce dependence on virgin raw materials. The industry is also moving toward automation. Manufacturers are developing automated sorting, shredding, and fiber-recovery systems to improve processing speed, consistency, and efficiency. However, fiber quality remains a key challenge. Repeated mechanical processing can shorten fibers and reduce their strength. Mixed and synthetic textile waste also complicates sorting and recycling. Asia Pacific held the largest market share in 2023 and is expected to remain the leading region. Its large textile manufacturing base, particularly in China and India, is supporting demand for recycling technologies, according to Transparency Market Research. Investment is expected to focus on automated sorting, high-capacity recycling systems and fiber-recovery technologies. Equipment that can process difficult textile blends while preserving fiber quality could gain importance as the industry moves toward circular production.

title: IsDB to provide $1 billion for Eastern Refinery modernization
summary: The Islamic Development Bank (IsDB) will provide $1.004 billion to support the modernization and expansion of Bangladesh’s Eastern Refinery, a project expected to significantly reduce the country’s de...
content: The Islamic Development Bank (IsDB) will provide $1.004 billion to support the modernization and expansion of Bangladesh’s Eastern Refinery, a project expected to significantly reduce the country’s dependence on imported refined fuel. Figure: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and Dr. Muhammad Al Jasser, Chairman of the Islamic Development Bank Group, attended the signing ceremony for the modernization of the Eastern Refinery. Courtesy: PMO The financing agreement for the Modernization and Expansion of Eastern Refinery in Bangladesh was signed on September 3 during the visit of Dr. Muhammad Al Jasser, Chairman, IsDB Group, to Dhaka. The agreement was signed between the Government of Bangladesh and IsDB. Dr. Mohammad Mizanur Rahman, Additional Secretary of the Economic Relations Division (ERD), Ministry of Finance, signed the agreement for Bangladesh, while Anasse Aissami, Director General, Country Programs, IsDB, signed for the development bank. The project will be implemented by Bangladesh Petroleum Corporation (BPC) under the Energy and Mineral Resources Division. The expansion will raise Eastern Refinery’s annual refining capacity from 1.5 million metric tons to 4.5 million metric tons. The upgraded refinery is also expected to produce Euro-5 standard petroleum products, supporting cleaner fuel use and improved environmental performance. The project comes at a time when Bangladesh remains heavily dependent on imported refined fuel. Increasing domestic refining capacity could therefore help reduce import exposure, strengthen energy security, and improve resilience against global fuel price and supply shocks. title: Global garment trade hits $546.8 billion as synthetic fibers gain ground
title_ko: 합성 섬유가 성장하면서 글로벌 의류 무역은 5,468억 달러를 기록했습니다.
summary: Global knit and woven garment exports reached $546.8 billion in 2025. The market has also changed significantly. Synthetic fibers are gaining a larger share. Bangladesh and Vietnam have also become ma...
content: Global knit and woven garment exports reached $546.8 billion in 2025. The market has also changed significantly. Synthetic fibers are gaining a larger share. Bangladesh and Vietnam have also become major players alongside China. Figure: Cotton’s share of global fiber demand fell from 68.3% in 1960 to 21.1% in 2025. Synthetic fibers moved in the opposite direction. Their share increased from 4.6% to 71.7% during the same period. According to the August 2026 issue of The Textiles Observer, published by the International Cotton Advisory Committee (ICAC), global textile exports grew from about $560 billion in 2006 to $914 billion in 2025. Knit and woven garment exports rose from $303.7 billion to $546.8 billion during the same period. This was an 80% increase. Knit garment exports reached $289.1 billion in 2025. They were $145.2 billion in 2006. Woven garment exports also grew. They increased from $158.5 billion to $257.7 billion. Together, knit and woven garments made up nearly 60% of global textile exports in 2025. Bangladesh moves up The growth has changed the global competitive landscape. China remained the world’s largest textile and garment exporter. Bangladesh made a major jump. It moved from 14 th place in 2006 to second in 2025. Vietnam also moved up. It rose from 21 st place to third. Together, China, Bangladesh and Vietnam accounted for about 44% of global textile exports in 2025. For Bangladesh, this shows its strong position in global apparel. But another major shift is taking place. Future growth is increasingly moving toward products that use man-made and synthetic fibers. title: London startup develops bio-based alternative to PFAS textile coatings
title_ko: 런던 스타트업, PFAS 텍스타일 코팅의 대안으로 bio-based 개발
summary: London-based Demeter Bio has developed a bio-based coating that could help textile manufacturers replace per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) without turning to microplastic-based alternatives....
content: London-based Demeter Bio has developed a bio-based coating that could help textile manufacturers replace per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) without turning to microplastic-based alternatives. Figure: From left to right - Caitlin Byrne, Adelya Khayrova, Emmanuel Asare, and Rayan Osseiran from the Demeter Bio team The company’s Fibrepel, formerly known as AguaShield, is designed to provide water and stain repellency for textiles and packaging. It can be used in applications including clothing, upholstery, hygiene products and packaging. Demeter Bio won the environment category of the Royal Society of Chemistry’s (RSC) 2026 Emerging Technologies Competition for the technology. The company began developing Fibrepel in 2024 as PFAS restrictions increased across Europe. Its founders said they found that some PFAS-free alternatives relied on microplastics and did not offer strong oil and alcohol resistance. Fibrepel uses biomaterials to target these performance gaps while avoiding PFAS and fluorinated chemistry. Demeter Bio says the technology can be adapted for different products and has potential for wider industrial applications. Rayan Osseiran, Co-Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Demeter Bio, said the technology is designed to support a shift toward PFAS-free materials rather than focusing only on removing PFAS from the environment.

title: Govt eases import rules for capital machinery, spare parts
summary: The government has updated regulations to ease imports of capital machinery, industrial spare parts, and consumer glassware. The move aims to boost investment and streamline trade operations. The prov...
content: The government has updated regulations to ease imports of capital machinery, industrial spare parts, and consumer glassware. The move aims to boost investment and streamline trade operations. The provisions were published in an extra edition of the Bangladesh Gazette on August 24, 2026. The updated rules provide greater flexibility for approved industrial enterprises while retaining quality, safety and risk-management measures. Courtesy: Collected Under Section 31 of the directive, approved industrial units will be able to import capital machinery based on the approved list issued by their sponsoring authority without obtaining an Import Registration Certificate (IRC). Foreign shareholders, NRBs, and foreign investors in approved industries may import capital machinery, spare parts, and raw materials with sponsoring authority approval. Payments from equity capital will remain subject to existing foreign exchange regulations. The new provisions also allow industrial units to import maintenance spare parts with approval from the Ministry of Commerce. The permissible annual import value will be linked to the total value of capital machinery installed in the facility. The allowance will be 2% of the capital machinery value during the first and second years, 1.5% in the third year and 2% annually from the fourth year onward. The directive has also introduced measures to simplify product clearance while maintaining quality standards. Products certified under Bangladesh Standards (BDS) by accredited laboratories, as well as products from companies holding valid Certification Marks (CM) licenses from relevant authorities, will be exempt from routine compulsory testing. However, customs authorities will retain the right to conduct random sampling under risk-management procedures

title: EURATEX urges meaningful import fee
summary: The European textile and clothing industry is calling for a meaningful handling fee on low-value imports to help cover the costs associated with the rapid growth of ultra-fast-fashion parcels entering the European Union Speaking at Première Vision Paris, EURATEX welcomed the introduction of a €3 customs duty on low-value imports and the abolition of the […] The post EURATEX urges meaningful import fee appeared first on Knitting Industry .
content: The European textile and clothing industry is calling for a meaningful handling fee on low-value imports to help cover the costs associated with the rapid growth of ultra-fast-fashion parcels entering the European Union Speaking at Première Vision Paris, EURATEX welcomed the introduction of a €3 customs duty on low-value imports and the abolition of the €150 customs duty exemption as important steps towards addressing what it describes as distortions in the European market. However, the organisation believes these measures should represent the beginning rather than the end of efforts to establish a level playing field for European textile and clothing manufacturers. EURATEX is proposing a handling fee in the region of €10 per parcel, arguing that this would more realistically reflect the costs generated by billions of direct-to-consumer shipments entering the Single Market each year. Every parcel entering the EU creates costs for customs authorities, which must process declarations, carry out risk assessments and verify compliance. Market surveillance authorities also require resources to identify unsafe and non-compliant goods, while product safety checks, logistics handling and enforcement activities add further costs. According to EURATEX, a significant proportion of these costs is currently borne by taxpayers and European companies that already comply with EU regulations. The organisation argues that the issue should therefore be considered primarily in terms of enforcement rather than simply trade or taxation. Revenue raised through a handling fee should be directly linked to strengthening customs controls, market surveillance, product safety enforcement and risk-analysis capabilities across the EU. content: Visual colour assessment has always depended on one fundamental requirement: standardisation. Whether colour is being evaluated by a brand, manufacturer, supplier, or testing laboratory, everyone needs to assess the product under consistent and repeatable lighting conditions. Organisations transitioning towards LED technology are facing new challenges when trying to ensure visual colour assessment is consistent throughout their supply chain. VeriVide has spent more than 60 years developing controlled lighting solutions for visual colour assessment. Their latest development expands the UltraView range, now offering two sizes so organisations have greater choice over how they can introduce LED colour assessment into their workflows. One Technology Two Sizes The launch of UltraView60 expands VeriVide’s current colour assessment cabinet range, and renames its current UltraView to UltraView90, making the distinction between the two sizes clear. UltraView60 provides a compact and cost-effective solution, while UltraView90 provides a larger viewing area. Both models deliver the same UltraView features and colour assessment capabilities, meaning organisations can choose the size and viewing area that best suits their workflow without sacrificing functionality. Businesses that do not require the larger viewing area of UltraView90 now have an alternative, cost effective entry into the range. This means that tuneable LED colour assessment is now more accessible than ever and provides greater flexibility when specifying equipment at different stages or locations throughout the supply chain. summary: A major investment in new wool scouring technology is taking shape at Standard Wool’s Thomas Chadwick & Sons operation in Dewsbury, West Yorkshire, strengthening one of the increasingly scarce industrial links between Britain’s sheep farms and its textile manufacturing sector. Installation of the new equipment has been progressing throughout the summer at Eastfield Mills, where […] The post Standard Wool investing in UK wool processing’s future appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: A major investment in new wool scouring technology is taking shape at Standard Wool’s Thomas Chadwick & Sons operation in Dewsbury, West Yorkshire, strengthening one of the increasingly scarce industrial links between Britain’s sheep farms and its textile manufacturing sector. Installation of the new equipment has been progressing throughout the summer at Eastfield Mills, where Thomas Chadwick & Sons has been processing wool since 1864. Standard Wool’s latest update, issued on August 27th, shows the scale of the work now underway as the company moves towards commissioning. Large-scale wool scouring capacity has become increasingly concentrated internationally, with much of the world’s raw wool now shipped to China for cleaning and subsequent processing. Essential first stage Scouring is the essential first industrial processing stage after wool has been removed from the sheep. Raw or greasy wool contains wool grease, dirt, salts, dust and other contaminants which must be removed before the fibre can move on to subsequent textile processes. The operation involves continuously passing the wool through a series of washing and rinsing bowls before drying and further cleaning. Typically, contaminants can account for some 35-40% of the weight of greasy wool, making effective scouring critical to both the quality and economics of subsequent processing. © Standard Wool It is also an energy, water and capital-intensive operation requiring considerable specialist expertise – factors which have contributed to the migration of much of the world’s scouring capacity towards larger international processing centres. With around 1,300 manufacturers from approximately 35 countries, […] The post “17 Bangladeshi Companies Strengthen Global Presence at Texworld & Apparel Sourcing Paris 2026” appeared first on Textile Focus .
content: Texworld Apparel Sourcing Paris, Europe’s premier trade fair for the textile and apparel industries, concluded successfully at Paris-Le Bourget. Held from 31 August to 2 September 2026, the 59th edition brought together international exhibitors, buyers, and industry professionals from across the global textile and fashion value chain. With around 1,300 manufacturers from approximately 35 countries , the fair brought together leading markets including Bangladesh, Pakistan, China, India, Türkiye, Myanmar, South Korea, Japan, and Italy , strengthening international sourcing and business connections. Bangladesh reinforced its position as the world’s second-largest sourcing hub for finished apparel after China, highlighting the country’s growing role in the global apparel supply chain and its strong manufacturing and export capabilities. 17 exhibitors from Bangladesh participated in the fair, showcasing the country’s diverse textile and apparel capabilities. The participating companies were Bnm Garments Industry, Bengal Glory, Comoda Garments, Corus Fashion, Dk Textile, Ducati Apparels, Fabitex Industries, Fabrica Knit Composite, H&f Fashion, Hoorain High Tech (Htf), Nexgen Apparel, Norban Comtex, Nz Denim, Nz Fabric, Sim Fabrics, Skylark Knit Composite, and Warptex. Bangladeshi exhibitors presented their latest products and capabilities to international buyers and visitors, gaining opportunities to develop new business relationships, explore emerging sourcing markets, and expand their global reach. Their participation further strengthened Bangladesh’s visibility as a competitive and reliable sourcing destination within the international textile and apparel industry. content: GREENSBORO, N.C. — September 3, 2026 — Cone Denim, a global denim innovator, today announced strategic transformation plans designed to better serve the global denim fabric market. The plans include strengthening Cone Denim’s focus on its established manufacturing platform in Mexico and the planned exit of denim manufacturing operations in China by year-end 2026. This repositioning follows a comprehensive review of the global denim market, Cone’s manufacturing footprint, customer sourcing needs, and long-term business strategy. The decision follows careful consideration of economic, market, and geopolitical factors that have increasingly affected the competitiveness and long-term sustainability of operating denim manufacturing in China. Changing global trade dynamics, evolving customer sourcing strategies, cost pressures, supply chain considerations, and broader geopolitical developments all contributed to this determination. “We are positioning Cone Denim for its next chapter of success, with a clear priority to continue delivering for our customers with the quality, innovation, reliability, and service that have defined Cone Denim for generations,” said Steve Maggard, President of Cone Denim. “Closing the China facility was a difficult but necessary decision as we position Cone Denim for long-term competitiveness in a changing global market. title: President urges swift resolution of RMG sector challenges
summary: President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir has called for swift measures to resolve the longstanding problems facing Bangladesh’s ready-made garment (RMG) export sector. He made the remarks on Wednesday du...
content: President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir has called for swift measures to resolve the longstanding problems facing Bangladesh’s ready-made garment (RMG) export sector. He made the remarks on Wednesday during a courtesy call by a BGMEA delegation led by President Mahmud Hasan Khan. The meeting underscored industry concerns and ongoing dialogue with government leadership. “The government is working to address the mismanagement and irregularities that have persisted in the country’s garment industry for a long time. Utmost efforts are continuing to resolve the existing problems quickly,” the President said. During the meeting, the BGMEA delegation briefed the President on the challenges facing the RMG industry and sought his cooperation in resolving them. In response, he assured the delegation that necessary steps would be taken to address the sector’s concerns. The delegation also invited the President to attend the closing ceremony of BATEXPO 2026 as chief guest. The event is scheduled to take place on November 19, and the President expressed interest in attending. President’s Military Secretary, Secretary, Press Secretary and senior officials were present at the meeting. President’s Press Secretary Md. Sarwar Alam later briefed journalists about the meeting.

title: Bangladesh strengthens European sourcing presence at Texworld Paris 2026
summary: Bangladesh used Texworld Apparel Sourcing Paris 2026 to strengthen its presence among European buyers as sourcing markets become more competitive. Seventeen Bangladeshi companies joined the three-day...
content: Bangladesh used Texworld Apparel Sourcing Paris 2026 to strengthen its presence among European buyers as sourcing markets become more competitive. Seventeen Bangladeshi companies joined the three-day event in Paris, showcasing garments, fabrics, denim and other textile capabilities while seeking new business opportunities. Figure: Bangladesh’s apparel industry leaders proudly representing their companies at Texworld & Apparel Sourcing Paris 2026 The 59th edition of Texworld Apparel Sourcing Paris was held from August 31 to September 2 at the Paris-Le Bourget Exhibition Centre. Organized by Messe Frankfurt, the event brought together manufacturers and sourcing professionals from around the world, with Bangladesh among the key sourcing countries represented. For Bangladesh, the participation came at an important time. The European Union (EU) remains the country’s largest trading partner, with textiles and apparel making up the vast majority of EU imports from Bangladesh. 17 companies represent Bangladesh The Bangladeshi delegation represented a mix of textile materials and finished apparel suppliers. Hoorain High Tech (HTF), NZ Denim and NZ Fabric participated in the Texworld section, while Nexgen Apparel and H&F Fashion joined Apparel Sourcing. Another 12 companies exhibited under the Export Promotion Bureau (EPB) Pavilion. They were Comoda Garments, Skylark Knit Composite, Norban Comtex, Warptex, BNM Garments Industry, Fabitex Industries, DK Textile, Fabrica Knit Composite, Ducati Apparels, Corus Fashion, Bengal Glory and SIM Fabrics. The companies used the platform to present their products, meet international buyers and explore new sourcing relationships. title: All About AI: Rupert Schiessl of Bamboo Rose
summary: Handing off the decision doesn't mean handing off control. Bamboo Rose’s Chief Strategy & AI Officer on why a governed digital workforce is the only safe way to let AI agents run the retail supply chain. The post All About AI: Rupert Schiessl of Bamboo Rose appeared first on The Interline .
content: Originally released in The Interline’s AI Report 2026 , this executive interview with Bamboo Rose is one of a 17-part series that sees The Interline quiz executives from companies who have either introduced new AI solutions or added meaningful new AI capabilities into their existing platforms . For more exclusive interviews, stories and opinions from different industry perspectives, and real survey feedback from voices from every level of fashion, download The AI Report 2026 . We’re observing a big disconnect (in both our own fashion-only data and in wider benchmarks from other sources) between the increasing capability and reliability of AI, in both a general sense and in discrete applications, and the lack of trust that end users place in its outputs. What does trust in your specific applications of AI look like, and how do you achieve and measure it? Trust in enterprise retail AI isn’t about blind faith; it’s about transparency and context. The trust gap exists because users are frequently handed “black box” recommendations without any visibility into how they were generated. If an AI tells a sourcing manager to switch suppliers or alters a demand forecast by 20%, the natural human reaction is skepticism. To break that down, we treat our AI as a performance co-pilot rather than an opaque decision-maker. We achieve trust through data lineage and identical governance. Our Metadata Layer (MDL) ensures that whether an AI agent or a human is looking at product data, they are bound by the exact same permissions, regulatory parameters, and compliance rules. title: Business leaders urge govt to fix energy crisis before seeking new investment
summary: Bangladesh’s textile industry leaders have urged the government to ensure reliable gas and power supplies to factories. They warn the worsening energy crisis is undermining production, exports, and ov...
content: Bangladesh’s textile industry leaders have urged the government to ensure reliable gas and power supplies to factories. They warn the worsening energy crisis is undermining production, exports, and overall competitiveness. They made the remarks at a seminar titled “Bangladesh’s Energy Security Challenges: Powering a More Competitive Business Climate,” jointly organized by the Metropolitan Chamber of Commerce and Industry (MCCI) and Policy Exchange of Bangladesh (PEB). Courtesy: Collected During the seminar, Showkat Aziz Russell, President, Bangladesh Textile Mills Association (BTMA) said that, gas shortages have become a major challenge for textile mills, many of which depend on captive power generation. He called on policymakers to formulate an interim energy policy to keep industries operational, while criticizing Bangladesh’s reliance on spot gas purchases instead of securing long-term contracts. Showkat said the country should have taken advantage of lower gas prices in the past by entering into long-term supply agreements, rather than depending heavily on spot-market purchases. He also questioned whether policymakers were adequately responding to repeated concerns raised by industry stakeholders. Fazlul Hoque, Administrator of FBCCI and Managing Director of Plummy Fashions Ltd., also stressed the need to stabilize existing industries before encouraging new industrial investment. Notably, the growing role of renewable energy in reducing industrial dependence on conventional power. One Factory invested around Tk 3–3.5 crore to install a 566kW rooftop solar system, which now meets approximately 25% of its peak electricity demand. title: Textile Genesis holds supplier workshop to understand platform usability
summary: Textile Genesis arranged an exclusive workshop today, bringing together suppliers to discuss their experience with the Textile Genesis platform and gather ideas on how it can be improved for everyday...
content: Textile Genesis arranged an exclusive workshop today, bringing together suppliers to discuss their experience with the Textile Genesis platform and gather ideas on how it can be improved for everyday use. The session drew a mixed group of participants, including traders and manufacturers, working with both sustainable and conventional materials — giving the discussion a fairly rounded picture of how different supply chain actors are using the platform. Speaking at the workshop, Textile Genesis Regional Lead Shahana Kiron said supply chain members are a key source of ideas for improvement, and that Textile Genesis is closely working to resolve supplier issues by arranging this kind of event. She added that the workshop itself reflects the importance the company places on supplier engagement. Throughout the session, Customer Success Manager Afroza Akter Shimu walked participants through the platform, sharing practical tips to help suppliers navigate common problems they face while using it. Figure: Shahana Kiron, Regional Lead & Advisor, TextileGenesis™. Suppliers responded to the initiative with enthusiasm, and several requested that Textile Genesis organize more in-person workshops of this kind, so they can continue engaging directly with their supply chain members. The day wrapped up with a group photo session, as participants exchanged thanks with one another before heading out.

The company says its latest developments have been designed specifically to address the challenges facing textile manufacturers […] The post Karl Mayer targets Asian growth in Shanghai appeared first on Knitting Industry .
content: Karl Mayer will showcase a wide range of new warp knitting, warp preparation and technical textile technologies at ITMA Asia 2026, combining two exhibition stands in Shanghai with a major product show at its manufacturing site in Changzhou. The company says its latest developments have been designed specifically to address the challenges facing textile manufacturers across Asia, where rising labour, energy and financing costs are being compounded by continued price pressure from international brands. Sustainability requirements, shorter lead times and smaller batch sizes are adding further pressure on margins. Karl Mayer will present warp knitting technologies in Hall 4.1, Booth C18 at the National Exhibition and Convention Center (NECC) Shanghai, while its warp preparation machinery will be shown in Hall 3, Booth A24. Further machine premieres will be demonstrated during an accompanying product show at Karl Mayer China in Changzhou. © Karl Mayer “Our closeness to customers in Asia helps us identify market requirements at an early stage and translate them into targeted innovations,” said Lutz Wolf, CEO of Karl Mayer. “That is why, at this trade fair, we will be showcasing solutions that are not only technologically leading but, above all, deliver one key benefit: they create measurable added value and long-term growth opportunities for our customers.” In warp knitting, Karl Mayer will introduce a new generation of tricot machines building on the cost-effective range that helped stimulate significant growth in the Chinese market during the late 2010s. title_ko: 맨체스터 패션위크 런웨이 너머를 바라보다
summary: Manchester Fashion Week returns with a four-day programme held from September 9-12 2026 across the city’s St John’s neighbourhood, uniting designers, brands, manufacturers, educators and innovators around an industry under pressure to change. The programme is organised around a set of problems the sector has been slow to confront. Rather than a schedule of trend […] The post Looking beyond the runway at Manchester Fashion Week appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: Manchester Fashion Week returns with a four-day programme held from September 9-12 2026 across the city’s St John’s neighbourhood, uniting designers, brands, manufacturers, educators and innovators around an industry under pressure to change. The programme is organised around a set of problems the sector has been slow to confront. Rather than a schedule of trend forecasting and brand showcases, the four days will work through synthetic fibre dependency, the economics of where clothes are made, who makes them and under what conditions, and what the industry’s rush toward AI actually costs. Changing Narratives opens the week on Wednesday September 9 th at the point of production, with ‘Near, Far and Number 10 North’ examining the balance between nearshoring, offshore manufacturing and supply chain resilience. The day will move through regenerative materials and next-generation animal-free innovation, before confronting the realities of fashion’s global workforce and how environmental progress can be made without displacing the livelihoods that depend on it. Changing Behaviour follows on Thursday 10 th with ‘The Polyester Paradigm’, exploring fashion’s dependence on synthetic fibres and the innovations attempting to break it. The day will move through repair, resale and take-back models, the independent businesses holding on to space in city centres, and the accessibility gap in adaptive design. Changing Industry on Friday turns to the systems beneath the product, from data and traceability in ‘The Data Thread’ to values-driven leadership in ‘Leading with Purpose’, and a series of sessions on how AI, 3D technology and automation are reshaping the way fashion is designed, produced and sold. ‘The Cost of Creativity’ will address the financial reality of building a career as

summary: Bangladesh does not grow cotton. Yet water may ultimately decide the country’s competitiveness in global denim sourcing. Before diving deeper, it is important to recognize that freshwater represent...
content: Bangladesh does not grow cotton. Yet water may ultimately decide the country’s competitiveness in global denim sourcing. Before diving deeper, it is important to recognize that freshwater represents only 2.5% of the world’s water, and we are doing everything with this limited resource. Of that 2.5%, only approximately 33% is available for daily uses such as drinking, washing, and textile processing. This apparent contradiction reveals a deeper truth about sustainability in textiles: carbon emissions in denim manufacturing are not generated in isolation, they are driven by water. Water that is pumped, heated, circulated, treated, and discharged consumes enormous amounts of energy. In Bangladesh, where denim production is heavily dependent on wet processing and fossil fuel-based utilities, water has become the hidden engine of carbon emissions. Following earlier discussions on carbon cost and environmental price wars in denim, this article explores how water management now defines carbon intensity, operational cost, and long-term viability of Bangladesh’s denim industry. title: Bangladesh exports rebound 13% in August despite energy crisis
summary: Key insights August merchandise exports rose 13.14% year-on-year to $4.43 billion. RMG exports increased 13.92% to $3.61 billion, led by knitwear. August exports fell 6.30% from July despite the ann...
content: Key insights August merchandise exports rose 13.14% year-on-year to $4.43 billion. RMG exports increased 13.92% to $3.61 billion, led by knitwear. August exports fell 6.30% from July despite the annual rebound. RMG contributed 81.47% of total export earnings in August. A low August 2025 base amplified this year’s headline export growth. Figure: RMG exports increased 13.92% to $3.61 billion, led by knitwear. Bangladesh’s merchandise exports rebounded strongly in August , but the headline growth masks a more complicated picture for manufacturers. Export earnings rose 13.14% year-on-year to $4.43 billion from around $3.92 billion a year earlier, according to the latest Export Promotion Bureau (EPB) data. The recovery came mainly from the readymade garment (RMG) sector, while several non-RMG industries also recorded double-digit growth. However, the monthly picture was weaker. August exports were 6.30% lower than July’s $4.73 billion. This indicates that the annual increase was not driven by a continuous month-on-month acceleration. Instead, a weak base in August 2025 played an important role in lifting the year-on-year growth rate. Table 1. Bangladesh’s RMG export performance in August 2026 Category August 2025 ($ Billion) August 2026 ($ Billion) Growth Rate (YoY) Knitwear 1.77 2.03 +14.88% Woven garments 1.40 1.57 +12.70% Total RMG 3.17 3.61 +13.92% Total exports 3.92 4.43 +13.14% Source: Export Promotion Bureau (EPB) and BGMEA. Together, the two garment segments accounted for 81.47% of Bangladesh’s total merchandise export earnings in August. The result is notable because manufacturers were operating under severe energy constraints. summary: The European Union’s Digital Product Passport (DPP) is creating a new opportunity for African textile and apparel manufacturers to improve traceability, circularity and access to the European market....
content: The European Union’s Digital Product Passport (DPP) is creating a new opportunity for African textile and apparel manufacturers to improve traceability, circularity and access to the European market. Figure:EU’s Digital Product Passport creates new opportunity for African textiles The European Commission launched the DPP Registry and testing environment on July 20, 2026, marking a major step toward making the system operational for businesses. The Registry will record unique product identifiers, registration data and key metadata, while detailed product information will remain with economic operators or their DPP service providers. For textile and apparel companies, the development is important because the sector is one of the EU’s priority product groups under the Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation (ESPR). The European Commission currently expects to adopt the textile-specific ESPR delegated act in the fourth quarter of 2027. A DPP could provide information on a garment’s product identification, fiber composition, origin, relevant economic operators, repair and maintenance, reuse, recycling and end-of-life management. A QR code or another data carrier on the product can provide access to the required information. For African manufacturers, this shift could turn sustainability compliance into a competitive opportunity. Better digital records can help exporters demonstrate product origin, material composition and environmental performance while building stronger links with European buyers. The opportunity is particularly relevant as African textile producers seek to expand their role in global value chains. title: Put a date on it: making textile EPR work in practice
title_ko: 날짜를 적으세요: 섬유 EPR이 실제로 작동하도록 만들기
summary: BY IWTO BRUSSELS – Two major pieces of EU legislation are moving into implementation at the same time, and textiles sit at their intersection. Member States must transpose the revised Waste Framework Directive, which requires textile Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) schemes to be established by April 2028. Meanwhile, the European Commission is developing textile-specific rules [...] The post Put a date on it: making textile EPR work in practice appeared first on Apparel Insider .
content: BY IWTO BRUSSELS – Two major pieces of EU legislation are moving into implementation at the same time, and textiles sit at their intersection. Member States must transpose the revised Waste Framework Directive, which requires textile Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) schemes to be established by April 2028. Meanwhile, the European Commission is developing textile-specific rules under the Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation (ESPR), including requirements for a Digital Product Passport (DPP). The two frameworks are designed to work together. Under the Waste Framework Directive, producer contributions are based on product weight and, where appropriate, quantity – the number of products placed on the market. These contributions finance collection, sorting, reuse, recycling and other end-of-life responsibilities. Fees must then be eco-modulated using relevant sustainability and circularity criteria developed under ESPR or other harmonised EU rules. This is an important step. But there is still a missing piece: evidence of what happens to garments in real life. Ecodesign rules are necessarily set before a product is sold. They therefore use tests, product characteristics and assumptions to predict durability, recyclability and likely lifetime. Yet technically durable clothing is not always worn for a long time. Fit, care, fashion cycles, price, resale and many other factors influence when a garment leaves use. Prediction is necessary, but it should not be mistaken for proof. A practical feedback loop IWTO proposes adding the year of production to the textile Digital Product Passport. Combined with statistically robust waste audits, this would allow authorities to see how quickly – or slowly – different categories of garments enter collection and waste streams.

content: By K. Positioned at the forefront of this transformation is ELİAR Elektronik, one of the world’s leading specialists in textile wet processing automation. With over four decades of innovation, the Turkish company has evolved from a manufacturer of electronic controllers into a comprehensive provider of intelligent automation, automated dosing systems and digital factory software. As ELİAR continues to expand its global footprint, India has emerged as one of the company’s most strategic markets, driving both business growth and long-term innovation. title: DeSL Launches Digital Product Passport Software Built on PLM
summary: New functionality enables brands to create, govern and publish Digital Product Passports using product, supplier, quality and certification data managed in DeSL PLM The post DeSL Launches Digital Product Passport Software Built on PLM appeared first on The Interline .
content: (New York, NY, September 2, 2026) Discover e-Solutions (DeSL), a provider of Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) solutions for the fashion, apparel, footwear and retail industries, today announced the launch of its Digital Product Passport (DPP) solution. The new functionality enables brands to create and publish Digital Product Passports directly from the product, supplier, quality and certification information managed within DeSL PLM . As Digital Product Passport requirements continue to develop, brands face the challenge of bringing together product information, material and supplier data, certifications, quality records and supporting documentation from across the supply chain. DeSL’s approach uses PLM as the foundation for managing and governing that information throughout the product lifecycle. Rather than creating a separate static record, DeSL generates each passport from the current approved information held within the platform. This allows information presented to consumers, retail partners and other stakeholders to remain connected to its underlying product and supplier records, including version history and approvals. The solution brings together product specifications, materials, supplier information, declarations, inspections and certifications. DeSL’s AI document intelligence can also analyze supporting documents, identify required information and expiration dates, and compare documentation against information maintained within PLM. title_ko: Print Tech Bangladesh 2026에서는 섬유 인쇄 및 인쇄 기술 솔루션을 조명합니다.
summary: The 10th Print Tech Bangladesh will bring printing technology suppliers, manufacturers and industry buyers together in Dhaka from September 24–26, 2026. The three-day trade show will take place at the...
content: The 10th Print Tech Bangladesh will bring printing technology suppliers, manufacturers and industry buyers together in Dhaka from September 24–26, 2026. The three-day trade show will take place at the International Convention City Bashundhara (ICCB). The event will showcase technologies and solutions for textile and garment printing, digital printing, screen printing and sublimation printing. It will also cover pre-press, print finishing, postpress, inks, consumables, software, labels and paper converting. The exhibition comes as Bangladesh’s textile and apparel industry looks to improve product value, flexibility and production efficiency. New printing technologies can help manufacturers meet demand for customized designs, shorter production runs and faster turnaround. Visitors will include textile and garment manufacturers, exporters, factory owners, purchase managers, production professionals, R&D teams, quality controllers, brand managers, label printers and packaging professionals. Print Tech Bangladesh has previously been held in 2023, 2024 and 2025. The 2026 edition will mark its 10th edition, bringing a wider range of printing and related technologies under one platform. With printing playing a growing role in apparel value addition and product differentiation, the exhibition is expected to offer Bangladesh’s manufacturers a platform to assess technologies that can support the next stage of industry growth.

content: Unimat, manufactured by James Cropper Advanced Materials, has been shortlisted for the CAMX 2026 Unsurpassed Innovation Award, recognising breakthrough technologies that advance the composites and advanced materials industry. CAMX 2026 – the Composites and Advanced Materials Expo – will take place from September 21-24, at the Georgia World Congress Centre in Atlanta, Georgia. Developed using Vectis, James Cropper’s proprietary fibre alignment technology, Unimat is a highly aligned discontinuous carbon fibre material engineered from recycled and production-induced waste carbon fibre feedstocks. It was developed through a strategic collaboration between James Cropper Advanced Materials and Carbon Fiber Recycling (CFR) in the UK, creating a scalable pathway for transforming carbon fibre waste into high-value composite reinforcement. The nomination highlights a significant industry achievement, demonstrating that recycled carbon fibre can deliver the performance, consistency and manufacturing readiness required for demanding composite applications, without sacrificing sustainability goals. Working alongside industry partners committed to improving sustainability within aerospace, Carbon Fiber Recycling applies its proprietary recovery and refinement technologies to transform carbon fibre waste into a high-quality feedstock. James Cropper subsequently uses Vectis technology to create up to 95% alignment in Unimat. “Through our collaboration with CFR, we have shown that recycled carbon fibre can be transformed into an industrially scalable material suitable for some of the most demanding composite applications,” said Lauren Wolstencroft, head of marketing at James Cropper. content: By K. Gopalakrishnan With a chemical portfolio spanning fibres, yarns, fabrics and garments, Resil Chemicals is strengthening its position as an innovation-led textile technology company. At India ITME, the company will showcase advanced solutions in textile finishing, technical textiles and sustainable processing, while highlighting the evolving convergence of chemistry, machinery and digitalisation. Ganesh Srinivasan, CEO, Resil Chemicals For Resil Chemicals, the future of textile chemistry lies increasingly in customization, technology and sustainability. As competition intensifies in conventional textile chemicals, the Bengaluru-based company is focusing on differentiated products, intellectual property, certified solutions and closer partnerships with brands and manufacturers. The strategy is already reflected in its portfolio. Resil is a major Indian manufacturer of silicone-based textile chemicals and resins, while its solutions extend across fibres, yarns, sewing threads, woven and knitted fabrics, garments and technical textiles. The company has also expanded into polyurethane chemistry, opening new opportunities in technical textiles and sustainable finishing. Speaking about the company’s innovation-led approach, Ganesh Srinivasan, CEO, Resil Chemicals, says “Competing solely on commodity chemicals and conventional technologies will not deliver sustainable, long-term growth.” he notes, highlighting the company’s focus on creating customized and “blue ocean” opportunities. Innovation at the Core Resil’s technology strategy is built around four pillars: product innovation, service excellence, sustainability, and trusted brand value. content: J.Zimmer Maschinenbau GmbH Klagenfurt and J.Zimmer Maschinenbau GmbH Kufstein | Digital Printing Systems have announced the launch of “Zimmer 2028”, a strategic transformation initiative that will unite the two operating companies into a single organization effective January 1st, 2028. Mr. Andreas Rass “Zimmer 2028” is our response to increasing economic pressure. It is a strategic organizational transformation that combines the best of two worlds. The demands of our market continue to evolve. Through this restructuring, we are not only responding to these changes but also creating the foundation to actively and successfully shape the future of our company. The objective is to align our organization consistently with the requirements of the years ahead, consolidate expertise, and create additional capacity for customer service, innovation, and growth. Changes with immediate effect: As of 31st August 2026, Horst Ros and Jürgen Scheriau have stepped down from their roles as Managing Directors. Horst Ros has left the company, while Jürgen Scheriau has withdrawn from the operational business and will no longer be involved in the company’s day-to-day management. We would like to take this opportunity to thank the departing Managing Directors, Mr. Jürgen Scheriau and Mr. Horst Ros, for their many years of commitment and valuable contributions to the company. We wish them every success and all the best in their future professional and personal endeavors. Effective September 1st, 2026, Mr. Thomas Mentler and Mr. Andreas Rass, who have already been serving as Managing Directors of J. summary: The 65th Dornbirn Global Fiber Congress (Dornbirn GFC) will open on September 16th in the Austrian town, with a high-level programme bringing together senior representatives from across the European fibres, textiles and nonwovens industries to address the technological, regulatory and economic forces reshaping the sector. Beginning at 9am in Hall A, the opening session will […] The post Industry leaders to open 65th Dornbirn GFC appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: The 65th Dornbirn Global Fiber Congress (Dornbirn GFC) will open on September 16 th in the Austrian town, with a high-level programme bringing together senior representatives from across the European fibres, textiles and nonwovens industries to address the technological, regulatory and economic forces reshaping the sector. Beginning at 9am in Hall A, the opening session will set the scene for the congress with perspectives on innovation, sustainability, circularity, European competitiveness and the continuing transformation of the fibre industry. Managing director of the congress, Béatrice Moureaux will officially open proceedings before Robert van de Kerkhof, president of the Austrian Fibers Institute, addresses the importance of innovation and the methodologies increasingly influencing the direction of the textile industry. A former Lenzing board member with extensive international experience in fibres and sustainability, van de Kerkhof will examine how developments including the European Green Deal and Product Environmental Footprint (PEF) methodology are helping shape future priorities for the industry. Demanding objectives The European fibre sector’s changing competitive environment will provide another major focus of the morning. Elke Hortmeyer of the Bremen Cotton Exchange will consider the challenges facing European fibres as the industry seeks to reconcile international competitiveness with increasingly demanding sustainability objectives, while Frédéric van Houte of CIRFS, the European Man-made Fibres Association, will provide the perspective of Europe’s man-made fibre producers. title: PI Cottex builds on Brückner stenter investments
title_ko: PI Cottex는 Brückner 스텐터 투자를 기반으로 합니다.
summary: India’s PI Cottex is planning further investment in finishing technology as it looks to increase production capacity from around 600 to 1,000 tons per month over the next two-to-five years. The Ludhiana-based company already operates four stenters, including two supplied by Brückner, one a six-chamber system and the other with ten-chambers, and says its experience […] The post PI Cottex builds on Brückner stenter investments appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: India’s PI Cottex is planning further investment in finishing technology as it looks to increase production capacity from around 600 to 1,000 tons per month over the next two-to-five years. The Ludhiana-based company already operates four stenters, including two supplied by Brückner, one a six-chamber system and the other with ten-chambers, and says its experience with the German machinery manufacturer is encouraging it to consider further installations as part of its expansion plans. “The reliable performance, high process reliability and consistently high quality of the finishing results gave us the confidence to invest in Brückner technology again,” says PI Cottex managing director Jasdeep Singh. He points in particular to the dryer design of the Brückner machines, which enables certain processes to be carried out with fewer chambers while maintaining the required results. Other benefits include high production output, consistent heat-setting, improved shrinkage control and reduced energy consumption. Control parameters The investments form part of the continuing development of PI Cottex from a traditional contract finisher into a vertically integrated knitted fabric manufacturer. The company now carries out knitting, dyeing and finishing in-house, providing control over parameters including colour shade, fabric weight and width, shrinkage and hand feel. Its portfolio includes single jersey, piqué, terry, fleece, rib, interlock and waffle fabrics, along with activewear materials, primarily based on cotton and cotton-elastane blends. It also develops fabrics to individual customer requirements in terms of weight, width, fibre blend, colour and finish.
