content: Ten innovators developing new technologies, materials and business models for the fashion and textile industries have been selected as finalists for the ninth Avantex Fashion Pitch. The international competition, organised by Messe Frankfurt France, culminates on 31 August 2026 with a Grand Finale in the Agora at Texworld Apparel Sourcing Paris. The finalists will present their solutions before a jury comprising investors, industry professionals and fashion innovation specialists. An evening event at Le Balcon, the rooftop restaurant of Galeries Lafayette, will bring together finalists, jury members, partners and invited guests, culminating in the announcement of the 2026 Avantex Fashion Pitch winner. Messe Frankfurt France launched Avantex Fashion Pitch alongside its Avantex Paris trade show to identify emerging solutions with the potential to transform how fashion is designed, manufactured and consumed, while helping their developers gain industry visibility and accelerate growth. The competition is open to start-ups, innovative SMEs, NGOs, researchers and entrepreneurs developing products, services and technologies for the fashion and textile industries, with a particular emphasis on B2B and B2B2C business models. This year’s finalists span services, textile and raw material innovation, and design technologies. YAWYA, founded by Shikha Shah, is developing a body-scanning solution combined with an automated fitting service aimed at helping designers deliver bespoke fashion. Seconde Matière, led by Angela Hertault, operates a B2B marketplace designed to facilitate the sourcing, resale and management of surplus textiles, leather and fashion components. content: On September 24 th 2026 at 10am, the organisers of the ITMA 2027 textile machinery show will hold a live webinar entitled From Connected Factories to Competitive Advantage. As technology connects, more machines, processes, data and people across the factory, the next challenge is turning that connectivity into real business advantage. Industry leaders will explore how automation and digital innovation can improve productivity, quality, agility and operational resilience, and how manufacturers can make smarter technology investment decisions. Participants can register here . The rise of the intelligent garment factory is meanwhile the subject of the latest ITMA Blog. Automation challenge Walk into one of today’s large apparel factories and you’ll witness autonomous vehicles, intelligent transport systems, automated warehouses, machine vision and AI-driven production planning. Yet at the centre of all this technology remains a surprisingly familiar sight – banks of operators guiding fabrics through sewing machines. Joining two pieces of textile together continues to be one of manufacturing’s hardest automation challenges. Unlike steel, plastic or other rigid materials, fabrics stretch, wrinkle, distort and behave differently depending on their construction, weight and finish. Humans instinctively compensate for these variations. Robots still struggle. As a result, sewing remains the most labour-intensive stage of garment production and depending on the complexity of the products being made, typically accounts for between 30-50% of the workforce within a vertically integrated garment factory, according to industry studies by Better Work, the International Labour Organization (ILO) and apparel manufacturing researchers. content: OBERTSHAUSEN, Germany — September 1, 2026 — At ITMA ASIA in Shanghai, KARL MAYER will once again demonstrate that it understands the challenges facing the Asian textile industry – and will present tailor-made solutions. It will do so across no fewer than three stages: Hall 4.1, Booth C18 for warp knitting Hall 3, Booth A24 for warp preparation An accompanying mega Product Show at the company’s Changzhou site The Asian markets are among the most dynamic and innovative in the world and are a key part of KARL MAYER’s global strategy. Across Asia, rising labour, energy, and financing costs are compounded by continued price pressure from international brands. At the same time, sustainability requirements, shorter lead times, and smaller batch sizes are making the battle for margins even tougher. With its new machines and textile solutions for ITMA ASIA, KARL MAYER will directly address precisely these challenges. “Our closeness to customers in Asia helps us identify market requirements at an early stage and translate them into targeted innovations. That is why, at this trade fair, we will be showcasing solutions that are not only technologically leading but, above all, deliver one key benefit: they create measurable added value and long-term growth opportunities for our customers,” explains Lutz Wolf, CEO of KARL MAYER. The company will present its solutions to the challenges facing its customers at two exhibition booths in Shanghai. This approach will also allow KARL MAYER to engage with customers from both the warp knitting and warp preparation sectors within their own industry environment. The seminar featured Sk. Mamun Ferdoush, General Manager (Marketing & Merchandising), Masco Group, […] The post NTEC seminar highlights skills and career strategies for future textile professionals appeared first on Textile Focus .
content: A seminar titled “Beyond the Degree: Building a Successful Career in Textile & RMG” was held at Narsingdi Textile Engineering College (NTEC), focusing on career readiness, industry expectations and the skills required to build successful careers in the textile and apparel sector. The seminar featured Sk. Mamun Ferdoush, General Manager (Marketing & Merchandising), Masco Group, who shared industry insights and practical guidance on preparing for professional careers in the textile and RMG industry. The session focused on career readiness and essential skills in the textile and apparel industry, highlighting the growing importance of analytical thinking, effective communication, technology literacy, leadership, creativity and adaptability. According to the speaker, the evolving nature of the textile and apparel industry requires professionals to go beyond academic qualifications and continuously develop the ability to analyse information, communicate effectively, work across functions and adapt to technological and business changes. Strategic career planning The seminar also addressed the importance of developing a strategic career roadmap. Students were encouraged to approach career development as a continuous process involving self-assessment, lifelong learning, personal branding, practical experience and professional networking. The discussion emphasised the need for students to identify their strengths and career interests while developing the technical, interpersonal and professional competencies relevant to their desired career paths. Internships as a bridge to industry Internship preparation and industry exposure were also highlighted during the session. Internships were described as an important bridge between academic knowledge and practical workplace experience.

content: At the forthcoming 65 th Dornbirn GFC conference taking place from September 16-18, Brussels, Belgium-headquartered Resortecs will provide full details of the development project behind the Helium Loop Anorak for the Swedish backcountry ski apparel manufacturer Peak Performance. “Until now, performance products that combine multiple materials, such as natural down insulation, zippers and elastic trims have been nearly impossible to recycle due to the complexity of disassembly at end-of-life,” says Resortecs marketing manager Sofia Scevaroli. “The Helium Loop Anorak, which will shortly be manufactured in commercial quantities, proves that advanced design in collaboration with the right partners can create real change.” Heat dissolvable Resortecs is the developer of Smart Stitch – a heat-activated sewing thread that is suitable for a variety of applications, from consumer apparel to workwear, and has been exhaustively tested on various production line configurations. It is also compatible with every stitching machine available on the market and in different colours and tenacities to enable full creativity in design and high quality in manufacturing. summary: Bangladesh and China are set to launch a new two‑tier diplomacy and defense dialogue. The initiative follows Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s recent visit to China, aiming to further strengthen bilater...
content: Bangladesh and China are set to launch a new two‑tier diplomacy and defense dialogue. The initiative follows Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s recent visit to China, aiming to further strengthen bilateral ties. The proposed framework was discussed during a meeting between Humaiun Kobir, State Minister, Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Chinese Ambassador to Bangladesh Yao Wen at the Foreign Ministry in Dhaka. Figure: Humaiun Kobir, State Minister, Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Chinese Ambassador to Bangladesh Yao Wen. The two sides also agreed to work towards launching a foreign minister-level strategic dialogue, seeking to give greater institutional depth to Bangladesh’s relationship with China, its largest trading partner and a major development and infrastructure partner. Kabir described China as a “trusted friend and valued strategic partner” and reaffirmed Bangladesh’s commitment to the one-China principle. He also welcomed renewed momentum in bilateral relations and the elevation of ties to a “China-Bangladesh Community with a Shared Future”. During the meeting, Yao briefed Kabir on the outcomes of Rahman’s China visit, including the innovative of the China Economic and Industrial Zone (CEIZ), the signing of a commercial contract to modernize Mongla seaport and potential Chinese cooperation in establishing a Mongla export-processing zone. The CEIZ is expected to attract around 30 Chinese companies and approximately $500 million in investment, with the potential to create about 100,000 jobs for Bangladeshis. The proposed diplomacy and defense dialogue could broaden bilateral cooperation beyond trade, infrastructure and development to strategic and security-related areas. title: AAFA Applauds Congressional Passage Of Two-Year Extension Of AGOA And Haiti HOPE/HELP Programs
summary: WASHINGTON, D.C. — September 1, 2026 — The American Apparel & Footwear Association (AAFA) celebrates the passage of a two-year extension of the Haiti Economic Lift Program and the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA) by the House with bipartisan support. The vote (370-48), which occurred as part of the Continuing Resolution (CR) to temporarily […]
content: WASHINGTON, D.C. — September 1, 2026 — The American Apparel & Footwear Association (AAFA) celebrates the passage of a two-year extension of the Haiti Economic Lift Program and the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA) by the House with bipartisan support. The vote (370-48), which occurred as part of the Continuing Resolution (CR) to temporarily fund the government, provides for a crucial extension of both programs, which were set to expire at the end of this year. Once the CR is signed into law, the programs will expire December 31, 2028. For 25 years, AGOA has provided eligible Sub-Saharan African countries with duty-free access, strengthening American exports in textiles and agriculture and fostering a wide array of U.S.–Africa commercial partnerships. Likewise, for more than 15 years, the Haiti HOPE/HELP programs have supported both U.S. and Haitian textile industries by granting Haiti duty-free access for apparel and textile products, building strong business ties between the two neighboring nations. “We are grateful for the bipartisan, bicameral support these vital programs have received and look forward to President Trump signing the two-year extension into law,” said Beth Hughes, AAFA’s Vice President of Trade and Customs Policy. “Our industry remains firmly committed to these programs and encourages Congress to use this extension as an opportunity to modernize AGOA and Haiti HOPE/HELP and build toward a 15-year renewal. Long-term renewal continues to be the goal in order to encourage long-term investment, deepen trade partnerships, and strengthen industries at home and throughout the region.” AAFA has consistently urged Congress and the Administration to renew both AGOA and Haiti HOPE/HELP, offering testimony before the Office of the U.S. Trade Representativ

content: Texworld Apparel Sourcing Paris, Europe’s premier trade fair for the textile and apparel industries, opens today at Paris Le Bourget and continues until 02 September 2026, bringing together manufacturers, suppliers, and professional buyers from across the global fashion and textile industry. The 59th edition features around 1,300 manufacturers from approximately 35 countries, offering international buyers a diverse range of fabrics, apparel, accessories, and innovative textile solutions. Figure: Warptex Bangladesh showcases its products to international buyers at Texworld Paris 2026. The exhibition brings together key textile and apparel markets, including Bangladesh, Pakistan, China, India, Türkiye, Myanmar, South Korea, Japan, and Italy. Bangladesh further strengthens its position as the world’s second-largest sourcing hub for finished apparel after China, highlighting its growing importance in the global apparel supply chain. A total of 17 Bangladeshi companies are participating in the fair, with some exhibiting independently and others under the Export Promotion Bureau (EPB) Pavilion, representing the country’s strong textile and apparel sector. Among the participating companies are Hoorain High Tech (HTF), NZ Denim, Skylark Knit Composite, Norban Comtex, Warptex, BNM Garments Industry, Fabitex Industries, DK Textile, and several others. Illias, Merchandising Manager at DK Textile, said, “The response at Texworld & Apparel Sourcing Paris 2026 has been very positive so far. We are optimistic about securing new business opportunities and attracting a significant number of international apparel buyers.” Bangladeshi exhibitors are welcoming buyers and visitors from around the world, showcasing the country’s capabilities across the global textile and apparel industry. content: The Indian terry product manufacturer’s repeat investment highlights the role of finishing performance and local technical support in building long-term machinery partnerships. Kapoor Industries Limited has expanded its installed base of Biancalani AIRO®24 finishing machines to eight units across its manufacturing facilities in India. The repeat investment represents a significant milestone for Italian textile machinery manufacturer Biancalani and strengthens its position in the Indian textile finishing market. Kapoor Industries is one of India’s established manufacturers and exporters of premium terry products, including towels, bath mats, rugs and bathrobes. The company operates vertically integrated manufacturing facilities in Panipat and supplies international customers, primarily in the United States and Europe. As Kapoor Industries has expanded its production capacity, it has continued investing in the AIRO®24 platform to support the finishing requirements of its terry product lines. While an initial machine order can demonstrate interest in a particular technology, repeated investment provides a stronger indication of its performance under industrial production conditions. The presence of eight AIRO®24 machines suggests that the technology has delivered consistent results across multiple stages of Kapoor Industries’ expansion. AIRO®24 Supports Terry Fabric Finishing Biancalani’s AIRO®24 is designed for continuous, open-width tumble drying, softening and finishing of woven, knitted and nonwoven fabrics. The system uses controlled high-speed airflow to move fabric alternately through a treatment channel and against specially designed stainless-steel grids. title: New Zeneri collection based on stay-up sock technology
summary: Premium Bulgarian men’s sock brand Zeneri has begun commercial production of a new collection based on its patented three-zone knitted architecture, developed to prevent socks from sliding down the leg while maintaining comfort. The technology, protected by European Patent EP3998888, is the result of five years of research, development and testing. Zeneri says successive knitting […] The post New Zeneri collection based on stay-up sock technology appeared first on Knitting Industry .
content: Premium Bulgarian men’s sock brand Zeneri has begun commercial production of a new collection based on its patented three-zone knitted architecture, developed to prevent socks from sliding down the leg while maintaining comfort. The technology, protected by European Patent EP3998888, is the result of five years of research, development and testing. Zeneri says successive knitting structures and prototypes were evaluated before the company arrived at the three-zone construction now being introduced commercially. The patented architecture takes a different approach to conventional sock retention. Traditional hosiery typically concentrates elastic tension in the welt, creating a relatively narrow high-pressure band at the top of the sock. Zeneri instead distributes support across three knitted zones, with compression decreasing up the leg and a dedicated stability zone positioned at the ankle. According to the company, the ankle zone plays a key role in determining the position of the sock, allowing retention to be achieved through the knitted structure rather than through silicone bands or additional grip finishes. © Zeneri Materials coming into direct contact with the leg are laboratory tested before entering production. Elastic fibres are knitted so they remain wrapped inside the cotton yarn rather than running bare against the skin. Zeneri says this construction enables the graduated compression structure to retain its shape while remaining breathable and avoiding excessive tightness. The socks also feature hand-linked toes. The retention technology has enabled Zeneri to reconsider the traditional length of formal men’s socks. content: By K. Gopalakrishnan With a specialized B2B ecosystem exclusively for Technical Textiles, spanning raw materials, finished products, machinery, technologies and services, TechTextileHub is seeking to transform how the global technical textiles industry discovers, connects and conducts business Technical textiles is no longer a niche extension of the traditional textile industry. From healthcare and infrastructure to mobility, filtration, defence, agriculture and environmental protection, textiles are increasingly being engineered for performance, functionality and application-specific requirements. Yet, paradoxically, one of the world’s fastest-evolving textile sectors remains highly fragmented when it comes to discovering suppliers, technologies, products and specialized services. Mr. Karthik Kumar, Promoter & Director, TechTextileHub It is this discovery gap that TechTextileHub (www.techtextilehub.com) seeks to address. Launched in March/April 2026, the India-developed platform has been conceived as a dedicated global B2B digital ecosystem exclusively for technical textiles and nonwovens. In its first few months, it has already onboarded more than 90+ verified suppliers across the value chain and has established an MoU with the Indian Technical Textile Association (ITTA). Webinars, newsletters and knowledge initiatives are also being developed alongside the commercial platform. The ambition is much larger than creating another online directory. Jengard brings more than 25 years of successful sales and project management experience to his position at Schotex. Based in […]
content: HONG KONG — September 1, 2026 — Sustainable and high-performance textile and textile technology developer Schotex Global® Co. Ltd. announces it has named outdoor industry sales veteran Mats Jengard as its head of sales for the Nordic region. Mats Jengard Jengard brings more than 25 years of successful sales and project management experience to his position at Schotex. Based in Sweden, Jengard has served as sales manager for established outdoor performance brands, including Norrona, PrimaLoft and W.L. Gore & Associates. Designed in Switzerland, developed from European raw materials, and manufactured on European machinery, the Schotex Global collection pairs Swiss design heritage with the efficiency of Asian manufacturing. Schotex Global textiles range from its ACTIVE double weave constructions and FLEX single-layer textiles with exceptional 4-way stretch comfort to its TERRA natural fiber and technical synthetic blends and its SHIELD ultimate weather protection 2- or 3-layer laminates. “We see great potential for Schotex in Northern Europe with the addition of Mats to our team, and are excited for him to introduce our product offerings to the outdoor performance brands in his Nordic region,” said Schotex Co-Founder and CEO Gwen Hsu. “His deep experience with global brands, collaborative work style, and focus on guiding long-term partnership programs with exceptional customer service align perfectly with our company goals and working principles. He is also a passionate outdoorsman who understands exactly what our consumers need and look for in their garments.” Outside of work, Jengard enjoys alpine skiing, downhill biking, hiking, as well as golf. He resides in Trollhättan, Sweden, with his wife of 30 years, their kids and dog. Posted: September 1, 2026 Source: Schotex Gl

summary: LOS ANGELES — September 1, 2026 — Tiger Commercial & Industrial (C&I) has completed the sale of a portfolio of high-precision fabrication and assembly machinery and equipment (M&E), along with finished products and raw materials, from two U.S. plants. Conducted on behalf of the secured creditors, the online auction featured M&E from the former Alpharetta, Georgia, […]
content: LOS ANGELES — September 1, 2026 — Tiger Commercial & Industrial (C&I) has completed the sale of a portfolio of high-precision fabrication and assembly machinery and equipment (M&E), along with finished products and raw materials, from two U.S. plants. Conducted on behalf of the secured creditors, the online auction featured M&E from the former Alpharetta, Georgia, and Dallas, Texas, facilities of Auzmet, a national manufacturer of exterior building solutions such as composite metal panels, architectural façades and insulated wall panels. Schlebach Quadro+ standing seam rollforming system Tiger marketed a broad mix of equipment from the two facilities, including CNC routers, electro-mechanical plate shears, CNC folding machines, electro-pneumatic saws, and smart routers by brands such as Miller, Lincoln Electric, FomIndustrie, Schechtl and Schlebach. Bidders in the 415-lot sale vied for plant-support M&E and rolling stock by brands such as Kaesar, Chevy and Mitsubishi, along with raw materials and finished-goods inventory originally valued at more than $1 million. Tiger’s in-house auction and operations team leveraged its proprietary database of repeat buyers in composites manufacturing to drive demand across the offering, managing the entire sale and removal process across both facilities within a tight 30-day deadline set by the landlord. “Our years of experience with aluminum fabrication equipment—including large-format panel builders from AXYZ Automation Group and units from Schechtl and Durma—gave us the ability to execute and quickly monetize the collateral,” said Jonathan Holiday, Senior Director of Tiger Commercial & Industrial. “The end result was a robust recovery for the secured creditors in a fraction of the usual timeframe.” Posted: September 1, 2026 Source:

summary: TEMPE, Ariz. — September 1, 2026 — Economic activity in the manufacturing sector expanded in August for the eighth consecutive month, say the nation’s supply executives in the latest ISM® Manufacturing PMI® Report. The report was issued today by Susan Spence, MBA, Chair of the Institute for Supply Management® (ISM®) Manufacturing Business Survey Committee. “The Manufacturing PMI® registered 54.6 percent in […]
content: TEMPE, Ariz. — September 1, 2026 — Economic activity in the manufacturing sector expanded in August for the eighth consecutive month, say the nation’s supply executives in the latest ISM ® Manufacturing PMI ® Report. The report was issued today by Susan Spence, MBA, Chair of the Institute for Supply Management ® (ISM ® ) Manufacturing Business Survey Committee. “The Manufacturing PMI ® registered 54.6 percent in August, 1 percentage point below the July figure of 55.6 percent. The overall economy continued in expansion for the 22nd month in a row. (A Manufacturing PMI ® above 47.5 percent, over a period of time, generally indicates an expansion of the overall economy.) The New Orders Index expanded for the eighth consecutive month after four straight readings in contraction, registering 53.7 percent, down 3 percentage points compared to July’s figure of 56.7 percent. The August reading of the Production Index (58.3 percent) is 0.2 percentage point lower than the 58.5 percent recorded in July. The Prices Index remained in expansion (or ‘increasing’ territory), registering 71.1 percent, the same reading as July. The Backlog of Orders Index registered 51.8 percent, down 3.2 percentage points compared to the 55 percent recorded in July. The Employment Index reading of 51.2 percent is down 1.6 percentage points from July’s figure of 52.8 percent,” says Spence. “The Supplier Deliveries Index indicated slowing performance for the ninth month in a row after one month in ‘faster’ territory. The reading of 59.3 percent is up 0.4 percentage point from its July reading of 58.9 percent. title: Mailroom #1
summary: The first edition of The Mailroom, where we put listeners' fashion technology questions to industry friends and experts, as well as answering a couple ourselves. The post Mailroom #1 appeared first on The Interline .
content: Ben Hanson: Hey. Welcome back to The Interline Podcast. Grace is away at the beach this week, so in place of her quizzing me about the headlines, we’re giving over the question-asker’s chair to you, the listeners, for our first Mailroom episode. To be clear, we don’t actually have a real physical mailroom — we’re a remote company. And if we did, I suspect it’d be like the one from Elf, full of surly drunks rather than anything magical. But what we do have are email addresses and direct messages And for the last couple of months, people have been sending in questions that they’d like us to answer to those inboxes. Today, we’ve picked six of them. Some come from a single named individual, while a couple are questions we got asked multiple times, so we’ve rolled those up into one question that I’ve condensed and paraphrased. But I figured it’d be a bit of a dull format if I just fielded all six myself, and there’s also no way that I have the best answers to them all either. So I’m going to pick up two at the end of the show myself, because I can answer them directly from our own data and by extrapolating from interviews I’ve done recently. For the other four, I wanted to pair each question with an industry friend who I thought had the best chance of giving a complete answer to the listener’s original question, but who’d also be game for me using that question as a bit of a springboard to overextend my host’s prerogative and ask some follow-on questions of my own. title: Bangladesh RMG turns production data into a productivity advantage
summary: Key insights Digital nesting can improve material utilization by 2%–3%, extending productivity gains beyond the sewing floor. Bangladesh’s 40%–50% worker efficiency trails China and Vietnam’s 60%–70%...
content: Key insights Digital nesting can improve material utilization by 2%–3%, extending productivity gains beyond the sewing floor. Bangladesh’s 40%–50% worker efficiency trails China and Vietnam’s 60%–70%, highlighting significant room for productivity improvement. Snowtex Group reports up to 25% productivity gains after connecting around 10,000 sewing machines to digital monitoring. Sparrow Group reports 5%–10% productivity improvement from its partial digital monitoring deployment. JUKI’s JaNets reportedly delivered a 12% productivity increase at a Dhaka knitwear factory in 2025. Figure: A 2025 deployment of JUKI’s JaNets reportedly delivered a 12% productivity increase at a Dhaka knitwear factory, while Nidle sensors achieved gains of up to 10% at another facility. Courtesy:Collected Bangladesh’s garment industry is increasingly turning production floors into data-driven operations as manufacturers seek higher productivity, faster problem-solving and stronger global trade. Real-time monitoring is allowing factories to identify machine stoppages, idle time, defects and production bottlenecks as they occur rather than relying on manual reporting. The technology being adopted is primarily Internet of Things (IoT)-enabled digital production monitoring and Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES) . Sensors connected to sewing machines capture machine status, output, cycle time, and downtime. The system can link operator identification, while centralized dashboards provide real-time visibility into production and quality. This shift is becoming more important as Bangladesh’s productivity gap pressures its export competitiveness. title: Germany faces a circularity challenge as textile waste rises
title_ko: 독일은 섬유 폐기물이 증가하면서 순환성 문제에 직면해 있습니다.
summary: Germany’s textile recycling sector is facing growing pressure as rising textile waste, contamination and weaker reuse markets challenge the country’s circular economy. Recyclers are struggling with hi...
content: Germany’s textile recycling sector is facing growing pressure as rising textile waste, contamination and weaker reuse markets challenge the country’s circular economy. Recyclers are struggling with higher operating costs while demand for used textiles and recycled materials remains under pressure. Figure:The German Federation for Secondary Raw Materials and Waste Management (BVSE) is demanding a binding 30% recycled-content quota and reforms to extended producer responsibility (EPR). Germany consumes nearly 19 kg of textiles per person each year, equivalent to about 1.56 million tons of textiles annually. Around 1 million tons of textile waste are collected each year, highlighting the scale of the material flow that needs to be sorted, reused or recycled. The latest industry data shows that the quality of collected textiles has also deteriorated. Contaminants and non-textile waste in collection containers have increased from 10.8% in 2018 to between 15% and 20% today. Higher contamination makes sorting more expensive and reduces the share of material suitable for reuse or recycling. At the same time, the share of collected textiles designated for reuse fell from 62% in 2018 to 44% in 2023. Mechanical and material recycling increased to 35%, while thermal recovery, including incineration, nearly doubled from 12% to 21%. The industry is therefore calling for stronger economic incentives and policy support. The German Federation for Secondary Raw Materials and Waste Management (BVSE) is demanding a binding 30% recycled-content quota and reforms to extended producer responsibility (EPR). title: Randa Acquires UNTUCKit Brand And Operations
summary: NEW YORK — September 1, 2026 — Randa Apparel & Accessories (Randa), a global leader in apparel and lifestyle accessories, today announced that it has acquired the UNTUCKit brand and operations. UNTUCKit is a digitally native, New York-based menswear brand with more than 70 retail stores and a substantial e-commerce business. The transaction brings together UNTUCKit’s […]
content: NEW YORK — September 1, 2026 — Randa Apparel & Accessories (Randa), a global leader in apparel and lifestyle accessories, today announced that it has acquired the UNTUCKit brand and operations. UNTUCKit is a digitally native, New York-based menswear brand with more than 70 retail stores and a substantial e-commerce business. The transaction brings together UNTUCKit’s strong direct relationship with consumers and Randa’s financial strength and global reach to support the brand’s next phase of growth. UNTUCKit Storefront in New Orleans “We spent 15 years proving that a shirt built to be worn untucked could become a brand people trust,” said Chris Riccobono, UNTUCKit’s founder. “Randa brings something different: more than a century of relationships with the world’s leading retailers and suppliers, along with the global capabilities to help UNTUCKit reach its next stage.” Founded in 2010, UNTUCKit built its name on the shirt designed to be worn untucked and grew into a leader in men’s dress and casual shirts, with a direct-to-consumer footprint spanning e-commerce and brick-and-mortar retail. The transaction advances Randa’s strategy of building and investing in leading brands while moving closer to the consumer. “UNTUCKit did the hard thing: it built a direct relationship with the consumer, store by store and click by click,” said Justin Spiegel, President of Randa. “Randa will add capital, global sourcing and market-leading retail relationships to that foundation. Export revenues […] The post Brazil sets cotton export record appeared first on Knitting Industry .
content: Brazil ended the 2025/26 commercial year with record cotton exports, consolidating its position as the world’s largest exporter and reinforcing its role as a strategic supplier to the global textile industry. Between August 2025 and July 2026, the country exported 3,373,941 tonnes of cotton, an increase of 19% compared with the previous cycle. Export revenues reached a record US$5.3 billion, around 9% higher than in 2024/25, according to ComexStat data compiled by the Brazilian Association of Cotton Growers (Abrapa). The increase represents approximately 538,500 additional tonnes of Brazilian cotton sold overseas during the year. © Abrapa According to Danyella Bonfim, Market Intelligence and Analysis Coordinator at Abrapa, the performance reflects a transformation built over several years, supported by increased production and improvements in the quality, traceability and sustainability of Brazilian cotton. “Brazil has expanded its production and gained scale, while also making progress in quality, traceability and sustainability. This combination has strengthened the competitiveness of Brazilian cotton and, above all, international buyers’ confidence in the country’s ability to supply the market on a regular and consistent basis,” she said. Data from the United States Department of Agriculture, presented in Abrapa’s August report, showed Brazil maintaining its position at the top of the global cotton export rankings. The United States ranked second in 2025/26 with exports of 2.656 million tonnes, followed by Australia with 1.241 million tonnes. © Abrapa Brazil exported approximately 718,000 tonnes more than the United States, its principal competitor in the international market. content: OBERTSHAUSEN, Germany — August 27, 2026 — As part of her summer tour, North Rhine-Westphalia’s Minister for Economic Affairs and Climate Action, Mona Neubaur, visited Textilfabrik 7.0 in Mönchengladbach to experience the project’s innovations first-hand. Under the motto “smart and clean”, the visit focused on innovative technologies and sustainable alternatives for textile production – from smart jackets to the decolourisation of textiles using fungal cultures. Minister Mona Neubaur with T7 logo Photo:© Tomas Rodriguez Researchers from the Research Institute for Textile and Clothing (FTB) of the Hochschule Niederrhein and the Institut für Textiltechnik (ITA) of RWTH Aachen University presented Minister Neubaur, Mönchengladbach Mayor Felix Heinrichs and representatives of state politics with innovative technologies and processes developed as part of T7. Textilfabrik 7.0 is being established in the Monforts Quartier as a real-world laboratory where innovative technologies and production processes are developed, tested under real-world conditions and further advanced for industrial application. The goal is to foster economically viable, CO₂-neutral and circular textile production in the Rhenish Mining Area. The halls of the T7-Factory in the Monforts Quartier are currently being equipped with machinery. The innovations already developed were presented to the visitors at the Technology Centre for Textile Finishing at Hochschule Niederrhein. title: Why Europe needs a meaningful handling fee on ultra-fast-fashion imports
summary: Paris, 01/09/2026 – The introduction of the €3 customs duty on low-value imports marks an important milestone in Europe’s efforts to address the challenges created by the rapid growth of ultra-fast-fashion imports. Together with the abolition of the €150 customs duty exemption, it demonstrates that policymakers are willing to act when market distortions become impossible… Read more The post Why Europe needs a meaningful handling fee on ultra-fast-fashion imports appeared first on EURATEX .
content: Paris, 01/09/2026 – The introduction of the €3 customs duty on low-value imports marks an important milestone in Europe’s efforts to address the challenges created by the rapid growth of ultra-fast-fashion imports. Together with the abolition of the €150 customs duty exemption, it demonstrates that policymakers are willing to act when market distortions become impossible to ignore. But this should be seen as a first step, not the final destination. Today, at Premiere Vision, the European textile and apparel industry reinforced the belief the European Union must now introduce a meaningful handling fee that reflects the real costs generated by billions of direct-to-consumer parcels entering the Single Market every year. A fee in the region of €10 per parcel provides a more realistic indication of the scale required to support effective enforcement. Every parcel entering the EU generates costs. Customs authorities must process declarations, conduct risk assessments and verify compliance. Market surveillance authorities need resources to identify unsafe and non-compliant goods. Product safety checks, logistics handling and enforcement activities all carry a price. Today, a significant portion of these costs is borne by taxpayers and by European companies that already comply with the rules. This is why the debate should not focus solely on trade or taxation. The issue is enforcement. A handling fee should be designed to ensure that those generating these costs contribute to covering them. For that reason, the revenues should be directly linked to strengthening customs controls, market surveillance, product safety enforcement and risk-analysis capabilities across the European Union. content: Initiative held since 2015 adopts a new format in 2026, with two immersion rounds and expanded participation from brands, retailers, NGOs and research institutes The Cotton Brazil Dialogues concludes its 2026 edition after a series of technical visits to farms, cotton gins and reference centers, as well as workshops focused on Brazilian cotton production. A total of 50 participants from 14 countries took part in the field trips. The initiative is led by the Brazilian Association of Cotton Growers (Abrapa) and the National Association of Cotton Exporters (Anea), with support from the Brazilian Trade and Investment Promotion Agency (ApexBrasil). Held since 2015, the initiative adopted an expanded format this year, bringing together a broader range of stakeholders from across the textile supply chain. In addition to spinners, the program welcomed representatives from brands, retailers, non-governmental organizations (NGOs), research institutes and other strategic stakeholders. Of the 50 participants, 32 represented spinning mills, while 18 represented brands, retailers and NGOs. Two immersion rounds were held in July and August. This broader participation reflects an evolution in the initiative’s approach. Beyond presenting Brazilian cotton to traditional buyers, the Cotton Brazil Dialogues creates a space for direct exchange between those who produce the fiber and those who source, transform, research, influence and make decisions across the supply chain. The aim is to foster greater understanding of Brazilian cotton production, strengthen connections between producers and the global textile industry, and contribute to a more transparent and responsible supply chain. title: Nanollose targets commercial scale-up of Nullarbor lyocell
title_ko: Nanollose는 Nullarbor lyocell의 상업적 규모 확장을 목표로 합니다.
summary: Australian biomaterials company Nanollose plans to build and operate a pilot-scale microbial cellulose pulp facility in Western Australia to accelerate the commercialization of its Nullarbor lyocell f...
content: Australian biomaterials company Nanollose plans to build and operate a pilot-scale microbial cellulose pulp facility in Western Australia to accelerate the commercialization of its Nullarbor lyocell fiber. The company said the facility will help validate its microbial-cellulose production process at an industry-relevant scale. This replaces an earlier plan to develop pilot and demonstration facilities with external partners. Andrew Moullin, Managing Director, Nanollose, said the company is focusing its near-term strategy on scaling Nullarbor lyocell and proving the technology before moving toward larger commercial arrangements. After validating the process, Nanollose plans to explore licensing, joint ventures or potential sale arrangements. The company does not currently plan to invest directly in full-scale fiber manufacturing. Nullarbor produces microbial cellulose rather than conventional wood-based pulp. The technology aims to provide an alternative feedstock for regenerated cellulosic fibers such as lyocell.

summary: The global fashion industry’s greenhouse gas emissions rose 6.3% in 2024, after a 7.5% increase in 2023. The rise was driven largely by higher fiber production, especially polyester, according to the...
content: The global fashion industry’s greenhouse gas emissions rose 6.3% in 2024, after a 7.5% increase in 2023. The rise was driven largely by higher fiber production, especially polyester, according to the Apparel Impact Institute (AII). Courtesy: Collected Fashion-sector emissions reached roughly 1 gigatons in 2024, equivalent to the total climate footprint of Japan, highlighting growing concerns over the industry’s decarbonization efforts. Kurt Kipka, Chief Impact Officer at AII, described the trend as concerning and linked the increase to greater material consumption across the industry. He also identified cost and availability as major barriers to decarbonization, noting that virgin polyester remains cheaper and more widely available than recycled alternatives. Rising energy prices are adding further pressure. Kipka said volatility caused by the Iran war underscores the need for apparel manufacturers to reduce dependence on oil and gas by adopting renewable energy and onsite battery storage. The industry could also face significant financial consequences if emissions are not reduced. Separate AII research projects a 34% decline in fashion-sector profits by 2030 due to supply-chain disruptions and rising operating costs unless companies take faster action to cut carbon emissions. Despite the challenges, the report highlighted progress in corporate climate commitments. The number of apparel companies with approved science-based climate targets or commitments to establish them increased from around 100 at the end of 2021 to more than 700 as of June 2026. Several major fashion brands have also reported double-digit emissions reductions and increased their use of recycled fibers in garments. title: Made In Filo At Filo66: The Fabric Collection That Celebrates The Supply Chain
title_ko: Filo66의 Made In Filo: 공급망을 기념하는 패브릭 컬렉션
summary: BIELLA, Italy — September 1, 2026 — The eagerly awaited “Made in Filo” collection is once again on show at the 66th edition of Filo. The fabric collection is designed and created by Filo with the aim of showcasing the potential developments of the materials exhibited at the fair to Filo visitors. “Made in Filo,” […]
content: BIELLA, Italy — September 1, 2026 — The eagerly awaited “Made in Filo” collection is once again on show at the 66th edition of Filo. The fabric collection is designed and created by Filo with the aim of showcasing the potential developments of the materials exhibited at the fair to Filo visitors. “Made in Filo,” now in its fourth edition, is a unique initiative among international trade fairs. To implement it, Filo has taken on the challenging task of “going into production itself.” The result is a collection of fabrics created from materials provided by exhibitors, which emphasizes the technical aspects of both the yarns used and the processes employed. The project, along with Filo, involves exhibitors and several partner companies. This edition focuses on the three souls of “Botanica”, the theme of Filo66’s product development proposals, available on Filo website, filo.it. For “Spontaneous,” very simple yarns were used, but they lend a more natural feel to the fabric. “Expanded” embodies the concept of an Italian garden, with very subtle weaves and effects. “Hybridised” gives free rein to the imagination, with highly structured jacquards and much more technical yarns. The “Made in Filo” fabric collection will be exhibited at the 66th edition of Filo in an area specifically dedicated to research and innovation. A preview can be seen in this short presentation video here: https://filo.it/made-in-filo-la-collezione-di-tessuti-che-esalta-la-filiera/ The 66th edition of Filo will take place on September 15 and 16, 2026, at Fiera Milano Rho, Hall 24. In collaboration with the International Centre for Bamboo and Rattan (ICBR) and other partners, the development programme addressed […] The post SGMW industrialises bamboo fibre composites appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: China’s SAIC‑GM‑Wuling (SGMW) has introduced bamboo‑fibre‑reinforced composites into interior trim components across more than 20 of its production vehicle models, covering eleven part categories including headliners, seat back panels, trunk trim, sun visors and central floor carpets. In collaboration with the International Centre for Bamboo and Rattan (ICBR) and other partners, the development programme addressed three core technical areas – lightweight bamboo fibre manufacturing, fibre‑resin interface bonding and air‑flow/mechanical uniform fibre mat forming. SGMW has established a full industrial chain integrating bamboo growers, fibre processing bases, parts suppliers and vehicle assembly, and has achieved volume production of high‑performance bamboo fibre composite materials. The bamboo fibre composite is manufactured from locally sourced bamboo in Guangxi. An interfacial toughening approach using low‑melting‑point polymers improves fibre‑matrix adhesion, with stepped pressure profiles during moulding reducing void content. An air‑flow and mechanical spreading technique enables uniform mat forming for continuous production. The finished panels contain 75% or more bamboo fibre by weight, with a density around 0.5 g/cm³ which is significantly lower than conventional engineering plastics, and a flexural modulus of 257.3 MPa, meeting automotive interior requirements. A deep‑draw compression process enables forming depths exceeding 25cm, addressing the limited flowability of natural fibres in complex three‑dimensional geometries. The material exhibits near‑zero formaldehyde emissions, reduces carbon emissions by approximately 0.55 kg per kilogram of material compared with conventional plastics, and degrades more than 90% within 360 days under natural conditions. title: CreateMe Strengthens Leadership Team To Accelerate Commercialization Of U.S.-Based AI-Powered Apparel Manufacturing
summary: NEWARK, CA. — September 1, 2026 — CreateMe Technologies, an AI robotics company pioneering automated apparel manufacturing through advanced bonding and robotics, today announced three key leadership appointments as it enters its next phase of commercialization. John W. Jacobson joins as vice president of commercialization, Leslie Lambert as vice president of people & business operations, […]
content: NEWARK, CA. — September 1, 2026 — CreateMe Technologies, an AI robotics company pioneering automated apparel manufacturing through advanced bonding and robotics, today announced three key leadership appointments as it enters its next phase of commercialization. John W. Jacobson joins as vice president of commercialization, Leslie Lambert as vice president of people & business operations, and Ashley Nicole Stickler has been promoted to vice president of marketing & partnerships. The appointments strengthen CreateMe’s commercial, operational and brand-building expertise at a pivotal time, as the company advances from technology development and early brand partnerships into broader commercial deployment of its automated manufacturing platform. John W. Jacobson John W. Jacobson joins in the newly created role of vice president of commercialization, bringing nearly two decades of experience building businesses across retail and global manufacturing. He previously co-founded Luminara Worldwide, scaling the business to more than $100 million in retail revenue and 30,000 retail outlets worldwide within six years. In his new role, Jacobson will lead commercialization strategy and work with brands, retailers and manufacturing partners to move programs from development through scaled production. Leslie Lambert Leslie Lambert joins as vice president of people & business operations, bringing more than 20 years of experience building and leading people functions across manufacturing, retail and consumer brands, including Ampersand Brands, CIRCA of America, Sephora and Williams-Sonoma. At CreateMe, she will lead people and business operations and build the talent, organizational, and workforce infrastructure needed to scale CreateMe’s apparel manufacturing platform. title_ko: 폰드그룹 '픽넘버쓰리', 2일 성수서 K 뷰티 알린다
summary: 폰드그룹(대표 임종민, 김유진)의 화장품 사업부문 K-뷰티 컨셉 스토어 ‘픽넘버쓰리(Pick No.3)’가 9월 2일 서울 성수동에 그랜드 오픈한다.픽넘버쓰리 성수점은 한국의 전통 미학을 현대적으로 풀어낸 북촌 플래그십 쇼룸에 이어, 성수라는 지역의 특성에 맞춰 한층 젊고 감각적으로 선보이는 신규 매장이다.빠르게 변화하는 뷰티 트렌드와 새 브랜드를 적극적으로 경험하는 성수의 소비자층을 겨냥, 기존 K-뷰티 편집숍과 차별화된 큐레이션 경험을 제공할 계획이다.성수에서 국내외 관광객과 젊은 소비자들의 핵심 상권인 연무장길에 자리한다.서울
